articles.title: Public trust in Senate falls, House trust rises in Q2 – OCTA
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Public trust and satisfaction in the Senate declined in the second quarter of 2026, while both measures for the House of Representatives increased, based on the latest OCTA…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Public trust and satisfaction in the Senate declined in the second quarter of 2026, while both measures for the House of Representatives increased, based on the latest OCTA Research “Tugon ng Masa” survey.
In its survey report released on Thursday, OCTA Research said trust in the Senate declined from 44 percent to 41 percent, while distrust increased from 24 percent to 27 percent.
Satisfaction with the Senate’s performance also declined from 42 percent to 38 percent, while dissatisfaction increased from 27 percent to 32 percent.
Meanwhile, trust in the House of Representatives increased from 36 percent to 38 percent, while distrust declined from 33 percent to 28 percent.
As for satisfaction with its performance, the lower chamber saw an increase from 35 percent to 37 percent, while dissatisfaction declined from 35 percent to 32 percent.
The poll was conducted among 1,200 adult Filipinos from July 4 to 11, with a margin of error of ±3 percentage points at a 95 percent confidence level.
OCTA Research noted that the survey period overlapped with the leadership row and eventual change in leadership in the Senate.
It also coincided with the opening days of the Senate’s impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte, which convened as an impeachment court on July 6. /jpv

articles.title: Filipinos’ visa-free stay in Thailand shortened to 30 days
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Thailand’s 60-day visa exemption will be replaced with 30-day visa free stays for tourists from 60 countries including the Philippines starting September 15, according to the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Thailand’s 60-day visa exemption will be replaced with 30-day visa free stays for tourists from 60 countries including the Philippines starting September 15, according to the Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT).
Thailand’s Ministry of Interior published the measure in its Royal Gazette on August 31.

“From 15 September 2026, travellers previously covered by the 60-day visa exemption will instead be subject to the applicable 30-day visa exemption, 15-day visa exemption, Visa on Arrival, or other relevant entry arrangements, depending on nationality,” the TAT said in a statement.
Filipinos are among those eligible for visa-free stays of up to 30 days.
TAT also explained that those using 30-day visa exemptions may enter through land-border immigration checkpoints no more than twice per calendar year.
Meanwhile, Visa on Arrival only applies to passport holders from Azerbaijan, Belarus, and Serbia, and 15-day visa free stays only apply to travelers from Seychelles and Mauritius. /gsg

articles.title: AirAsia seals first codeshare with Pegasus, bridges Asia and Europe
articles.summary: AirAsia has signed its first-ever codeshare agreement, teaming up with Turkey’s largest low-cost carrier, Pegasus Airlines, to open seamless connections between Southeast Asia and Europe…

blocks.text: AirAsia has signed its first-ever codeshare agreement, teaming up with Turkey’s largest low-cost carrier, Pegasus Airlines, to open seamless connections between Southeast Asia and Europe through Istanbul, the two airlines announced at AirAsia’s headquarters in Sepang, Malaysia, on Wednesday.

The partnership, unveiled before members of the media and witnessed by Turkey’s ambassador to Malaysia Nevzat Uyanık, will progressively open access to more than 100 routes between Asia and Europe, combining AirAsia’s Southeast Asian network with Pegasus’s reach across Europe from its hub at Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport.

Five European destinations will be added from launch: Stansted (London), Vnukovo (Moscow), Esenboğa (Ankara), Zurich and Athens, all connecting through Kuala Lumpur and Istanbul. AirAsia will also lift its Kuala Lumpur–Istanbul frequency from four times weekly to daily by February 2027, up from the direct link AirAsia X has operated since November 2025.

blocks.caption: Farouk Kamal

blocks.text: Opening the event, Farouk Kamal, Deputy Group Chief Executive Officer of AirAsia Group Berhad, told guests the tie-up “marks the start of many more opportunities to come between the two airlines” and reaffirmed the group’s ambition to become the world’s first low-cost network carrier.
He said he had personally tried the product being announced on a trip last year and described the experience as “great” before handing over to colleagues to reveal the details on stage.

blocks.caption: AirAsia Seals First Codeshare With Pegasus, Bridges Asia and Europe

blocks.text: ‘Meaningful milestone’ in 25th year
In a statement accompanying the announcement, Bo Lingam, Group CEO of AirAsia Group, said the codeshare was a landmark moment as the airline marks its 25th anniversary.

“As AirAsia’s first-ever codeshare, this partnership marks a meaningful milestone in our 25th year and the next chapter in our evolution from a leading Asean low-cost carrier into a truly global travel network,” he said. “By connecting our extensive network across Asia with Pegasus’s strong European network from Istanbul, spanning 160 destinations across 56 countries, we are making Europe more accessible to our guests while creating a gateway for European travelers to discover Asean and beyond.”

blocks.caption: Elifnur Dogruoz

blocks.text: On stage representing Pegasus was Elifnur Dogruoz, the airline’s Group Head of Network Planning and Airline Collaborations, who told the audience the two carriers shared a common philosophy despite operating at opposite ends of Asia.

“At AirAsia your promise is ‘now everyone can fly.’ At Pegasus we say everyone has the right to fly – different words, but the same belief that air travel should be accessible for more people across more places,” she said, adding that Sabiha Gökçen was “more than a home” for Pegasus and a key gateway between Europe and Asia, just as Kuala Lumpur was for AirAsia.

blocks.caption: AirAsia Seals First Codeshare With Pegasus, Bridges Asia and Europe

blocks.text: She thanked Malaysia’s civil aviation authorities and airport operators for supporting the deal.
Pegasus chief executive Güliz Öztürk, who also did not attend the Kuala Lumpur event, added in a statement issued alongside the announcement:

“Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen is a natural connecting point between Europe and Asia. That AirAsia’s first-ever codeshare is with Pegasus Airlines is a source of pride: it reflects the network we have built from Istanbul over two decades and a hub that continues to grow. Our guests can now reach Kuala Lumpur seamlessly and, from there, AirAsia’s network of more than 140 destinations across Asia-Pacific.”

blocks.caption: Amanda Woo

blocks.text: Presenting the mechanics of the partnership to media, AirAsia’s Chief Commercial Officer, Amanda Woo, explained that travelers booking through AirAsia will receive both boarding passes at check-in, with baggage checked straight through to their final destination.

“One journey, one itinerary, a seamless experience,” she said, describing how a passenger flying from Kuala Lumpur to Athens via Istanbul would simply follow the signs to their next gate in Istanbul without needing to check in again or collect their bags.

Woo said the combined network would ultimately connect more than 100 routes between Asia and Europe and confirmed a further sweetener for early bookers: AirAsia will raise its Kuala Lumpur–Istanbul service from four times weekly to daily next year to meet expected demand.

The new connectivity also runs in reverse, with European travelers able to connect through Istanbul to Kuala Lumpur and onwards across AirAsia’s Fly-Thru network spanning Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, China, Vietnam and beyond. /dl

articles.title: P7.3-M ‘smuggled’ cigarettes seized in Zamboanga Peninsula ops
articles.summary: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – The Police Regional Office-9 (PRO-9) intensified its anti-smuggling campaign, confiscating at least P7.3 million worth of alleged illicit cigarettes in a series of…

blocks.text: PAGADIAN CITY, Zamboanga del Sur – The Police Regional Office-9 (PRO-9) intensified its anti-smuggling campaign, confiscating at least P7.3 million worth of alleged illicit cigarettes in a series of operations across Zamboanga del Norte, Zamboanga City, and Pagadian City from August 31 to September 2.

Maj. Shellamie Chang, PRO-9 spokesperson, told the Inquirer that in Salug, Zamboanga del Norte, operatives arrested a 47-year-old driver from Zamboanga City after intercepting a multi-purpose vehicle (Nissan Livina) loaded with 1,049 reams of alleged illicit cigarettes during a checkpoint in Barangay Canawan on September 1.
Salug Municipal Police personnel seized the contraband valued at P4,133,060.

On August 31, police discovered an unattended minivan along the highway in Barangay Bolong, Zamboanga City. The vehicle contained 48 boxes of assorted suspected smuggled cigarettes with an estimated value of P1,014,510. The items were turned over to the Bureau of Customs (BOC) District Office 9.

In Pagadian City, police operatives confiscated 13 master cases of alleged smuggled cigarettes worth P744,900 from a motorized tricycle locally known as “bao-bao” on September 1. Two suspects were arrested.

Meanwhile, on September 2, PRO 9’s Regional Intelligence Division and Regional Special Operations Unit recovered 25 master cases of smuggled cigarettes abandoned along the shoreline of Barangay Sinunuc, Zamboanga City. The haul was valued at P1,432,500.
All seized contraband and vehicles were placed under police custody and will be formally turned over to the BOC for proper disposition.
The arrested suspects face charges for alleged violations of Republic Act (RA) 10863, or the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act, and RA 10643, or the Graphic Health Warnings Law./coa

articles.title: BARMM polls: Maguindanao del Norte a key regional battleground
articles.summary: The election outcome in Maguindanao del Norte's 3rd district is crucial as it could determine the direction of the new Bangsamoro region

blocks.text: The election outcome in Maguindanao del Norte's 3rd district is crucial as it could determine the direction of the new Bangsamoro region

items: Abdulraof 'Sammy Gambar' Macacua is running for election in the 3rd parliamentary district of Maguindanao del Norte, which will determine his future as the leader of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

Macacua, a former acting governor and senior BARMM minister, has a significant political background, including leading the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces during the peace agreement that established BARMM.
The election results are crucial for the new Bangsamoro region, with Macacua facing challenger Badrudin Mamad in a competitive race, while other districts have varying levels of competition.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

CEBU, Philippines – Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) interim Chief Minister Abdulraof “Sammy Gambar” Macacua is running in the 3rd parliamentary district of Maguindanao del Norte where the election results could determine whether he stays or not as the region’s leader.
Before his rise to the BARMM top leadership, Macacua was officer-in-charge or acting governor of Maguindanao del Norte.
He was a senior BARMM minister before that under then-interim chief minister Ahod “Al Haj Murad” Ebrahim, the chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
Macacua led the MILF’s armed wing, the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forcea (BIAF), at the height of the Front’s struggle that resulted in a peace agreement in 2014 and the creation of the BARMM in 2019.
His appointment as acting governor of Maguindanao del Norte in 2023, caused a stir among the ruling Sinsuat and Mangudadatu clans of the old Maguindanao province, which was split into two.
His subsequent appointment as Murad’s successor also caused tensions within the MILF.

If Macacua wins in the September elections, he would be eligible and could be chosen by the BARMM parliament as the first elected chief minister of the seven-year-old region. This makes the election outcome in the Maguindanao del Norte district crucial as it could determine the direction of the new Bangsamoro region.
Based on the Commission on Elections’ database as of May 8, there are a total of 223 barangays and 419,518 registered voters spread throughout the province.
Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 86, which finalized the region’s 32 parliamentary districts, gave Maguindanao del Norte five seats.
Here are the electoral races happening in Maguindanao del Norte’s five parliamentary districts:

blocks.caption: MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE 1ST DISTRICT RACE. From left: Abdulkudos Pendatu Balitok and Prince Khalid Tomawis. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: The first parliamentary district consists of the towns of Matanog, Barira, and Buldon.
Abdulkudos Pendatu Balitok, a former base commander of the BIAF-MILF and ex-deputy minister for public order and safety, is running for the district’s parliamentary seat.
Balitok is the bet of the United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP), the MILF’s political party.
The former BIAF-MILF commander is up against Prince Khalid Tomawis of the Bangsamoro Federalist Party (BFP), the party founded by Member of Parliament Tomanda Antok.
Tomawis is the son of the late former Barira mayor Alexander Tomawis and former Buldon mayor Fatima Ruth Tomawis.

blocks.caption: MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE 2ND DISTRICT RACE. Member of Parliament Ibrahim Pendat Ibay. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: The second district covers the municipality of Parang.
Member of Parliament Ibrahim Pendat Ibay, the bet of BFP, is running unopposed in his home turf. Ibay is a former mayor of Parang and a former deputy interior minister of the BARMM.

blocks.caption: MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE 3RD DISTRICT RACE. From left: BARMM Interim Chief Minister Abdulraof Macacua and Badrudin Mamad. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: The third district comprises the towns of Northern Kabuntalan, Kabuntalan, and Talitay.
It also includes the barangays of Poblacion I and Poblacion VII in Cotabato City, and the barangays of Katamlangan, Nalinan, Kabuntalan, Kapimpilan, and Bulibod in Sultan Kudarat town.
Macacua is joining the electoral race here. In a MindaNews article dated May 7, 2026, Macacua, through his son Jamael Macacua, filed his certificate of candidacy as an independent candidate.
While he is classified as an independent candidate, Macacua currently leads the BFP after taking over Antok’s role as party president in August.

Initially, independent candidate Asnawe Bagundang Baraguir was set to join the district’s parliamentary race but he eventually withdrew his candidacy in May, according to Brigada News FM Cotabato City.
Macacua will be going up against Badrudin Mamad, another independent candidate from Barangay Libungan, Northern Kabuntalan.

blocks.caption: MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE 4TH DISTRICT RACE. From left: Former Maguindanao del Norte vice governor Abdulnasser Maliga Abas, former Maguindanao 1st district representative Bai Sandra Ampatuan Sema, former Upi municipal councilor Alexander Petalcorin Agustin, and Jashriya Sema Dilangalen. Photos from t…

blocks.text: The fourth district includes the towns of Datu Odin Sinsuat, Datu Blah T. Sinsuat, and Upi.
Former Maguindanao del Norte vice governor Abdulnasser Maliga Abas is running for the fourth district parliamentary seat. He is the bet of the UBJP.

Former Upi municipal councilor Alexander Petalcorin Agustin is running under the Bangsamoro Empowerment and Social Transformation Party (BEST Party) led by Al-Rashid Balt, the director general of the Bangsamoro Ministry of Public Order and Safety.

Former Maguindanao 1st district representative Bai Sandra Ampatuan Sema, the wife of incumbent BARMM minister of labor and employment Muslimin Sema, is also in the race as the bet of the Bangsamoro Party (BAPA). Muslimin is the head of BAPA.
Also in the race is independent candidate Jashriya Sema Dilangalen.

blocks.caption: MAGUINDANAO DEL NORTE 5TH DISTRICT RACE. Member of Parliament Ishak Veloso Mastura. Photos from their Facebook.

blocks.text: In the fifth district, which covers Sultan Kudarat and Sultan Mastura, BFP bet and Member of Parliament Ishak Veloso Mastura is running unopposed.
Mastura is a deputy speaker of the Bangsamoro parliament and the son of Michael Ong Mastura, a former representative of the first district of the old Maguindanao and Cotabato City. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Seven Thai airlines offer free 10kg fruit check-in at 20 airports
articles.summary: BANGKOK — Passengers can check one 10kg box of fresh fruit for free at 20 Thai airports under a year-long scheme that began on September 1. Seven airlines will allow passengers to check up to…

blocks.text: BANGKOK — Passengers can check one 10kg box of fresh fruit for free at 20 Thai airports under a year-long scheme that began on September 1.
Seven airlines will allow passengers to check up to 10 kilograms of fresh fruit into the aircraft hold free of charge under a year-long program covering 20 airports across Thailand.

The Commerce Ministry, through the Department of Internal Trade, has signed a cooperation agreement with the Transport Ministry’s Department of Airports and seven airline partners: Thai Airways International, Thai AirAsia, Bangkok Airways, Nok Air, Thai Lion Air, Thai Vietjet Air and EZY Airlines.

blocks.caption: Seven airlines offer free 10kg fruit check-in at 20 airports

blocks.text: The program will run from September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027, and is intended to help farmers distribute seasonal produce, encourage consumption of Thai fruit and support domestic tourism.

Banjongjitt Angsusingh, adviser to the commerce minister, said the government was seeking a wider range of distribution channels for agricultural produce entering the market. Her English name and title follow the Commerce Ministry’s official listing.

The cooperation would use the capabilities of airports and airlines to help travellers carry fruit home from producing areas and tourism destinations without having to pay additional transport charges, she said.

blocks.caption: Seven airlines offer free 10kg fruit check-in at 20 airports

blocks.text: One free 10kg box per passenger
Passengers using the service will be entitled to one standard fruit box with a maximum weight of 10kg.

The Department of Internal Trade will supply the boxes to participating airports from September 1. It will also work with provincial commerce offices to bring farmers into airport sales areas to sell seasonal fruit directly to travellers.
The Department of Airports will provide collection points for the boxes, assist passengers using the service and allocate temporary sales spaces for farmers at airports under its supervision.
The seven partner airlines will carry the fruit in their aircraft holds free of charge, subject to the 10kg limit per passenger, and promote the programme through their communication channels.
EZY Airlines is the official branding used by the participating Thai regional carrier.

blocks.caption: Seven airlines offer free 10kg fruit check-in at 20 airports

blocks.text: Twenty airports join pilot programme
The service will initially be available at airports in:

Nan, Lampang, Tak, Phitsanulok, Loei, Udon Thani, Khon Kaen, Sakon Nakhon, Nakhon Phanom, Roi Et, Ubon Ratchathani, Buri Ram, Prachuap Khiri Khan, Chumphon, Ranong, Surat Thani, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Krabi, Trang and Narathiwat.
Passengers should contact the designated service point at the airport to receive their fruit box before checking it into the hold.
The authorities initially aim to distribute 100,000 boxes, representing capacity for approximately 1,000 tonnes of fruit.

blocks.caption: Seven airlines offer free 10kg fruit check-in at 20 airports

blocks.text: Fresh fruit only, with strict packaging rules
Only fresh fruit will be accepted under the programme. The total weight must not exceed 10kg, and the fruit must be dry and free from moisture.

Passengers must use the official box supplied by the Department of Internal Trade at the airport service point. The container must be securely closed with adhesive tape or straps to prevent ants, insects and foreign objects from entering, as well as to stop liquid or odours from escaping.
Durian and other strongly scented fruit will not be accepted either in the cabin or as checked baggage because their smell could disturb other passengers.
“Before bringing fruit on a flight, passengers should ensure that it is packed properly,” Banjongjitt said.

“Durian and other strongly scented fruit must not be carried on board or placed in the aircraft hold, so that the smell does not disturb other passengers and everyone can enjoy a convenient and smooth journey.” /dl

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — Six Baguio residents were evacuated on Thursday after a landslide damaged a house at Purok 3 in Barangay Guisad Surong, where a much bigger August 9 erosion killed 10 people, the Baguio City Police Office (BCPO) said.
Police helped relocate the six affected residents to a pastor’s house in Purok 4.
Authorities said they will install temporary covering and other protective measures at the affected site to prevent further soil erosion.
Residents in landslide-prone areas were advised to stay vigilant and immediately move to safer areas when conditions become hazardous. Maureen Matayew/Contributor/coa

articles.title: DepEd holds simultaneous school safety drills nationwide
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) on Thursday conducted the National Simultaneous School Safety Drill.

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 10:51am
The Department of Education (DepEd) on Thursday conducted the National Simultaneous School Safety Drill.

In a statement, the DepEd said the drill was held to strengthen schools' preparedness and response capacity for active threat scenarios and other emergencies under the School Safety Contingency Plans.

Safety drills were conducted in schools across the country, including the Carlos F. Gonzales High School in Bulacan, which was attended by Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, DepEd Undersecretary Malcolm Garma, and Assistant Secretary Jocelyn Andaya.
Earlier, Deped said the drill was designed to promote preparedness and build students' and school personnel's procedural "muscle memory" without creating fear or trauma.
The department said it coordinated with medical and mental health organizations to ensure the exercise follows child-centered and trauma-informed standards.
DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara said that physical security and mental health should be treated as equally important in school safety.
"Safety is not just about physical security; it is equally about protecting our children's peace of mind," Angara said.
During the exercise, learners practiced protective actions such as securing entry points, silent concealment away from windows, and reviewing evacuation routes.

DepEd said the drill strictly prohibited hyper-realistic or fear-inducing elements, including active aggressor role-players, weapons, simulated gunfire, pyrotechnics, firearms, and artificial casualties.
The activity was conducted after the fatal shootings in Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City on August 18 and San Jose National High School in Tacloban City on June 22. —VAL, GMA News

articles.summary: Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says two whales have died after it took in several beluga whales from Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont.

image.caption: A beluga whale swims in a tank at Marineland before being moved to an aquarium in the U.S. on Monday. Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says two whales, including one from Marineland, died today. (Carlos Osorio/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Canada·New
Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says two whales have died after it took in several beluga whales from Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont.
Beluga was one of 2 that died at Shedd Aquarium Wednesday
· The Canadian Press
· Posted: Sep 02, 2026 10:48 PM EDT | Last Updated: 12 minutes ago
Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says two whales have died after it took in 10 beluga whales from Marineland in Niagara Falls, Ont.
Shedd says one whale, Rain, came from Marineland in mid-August while the other, Beethoven, was already a resident.
Marineland, along with Shedd and several other aquariums, recently completed an unprecedented relocation of captive whales after shipping 30 belugas and four dolphins to five destinations.
Another Marineland beluga, Peekachu, died last week after it became severely dehydrated.
Shedd says the deaths occurred Wednesday afternoon despite immediately trying to save the whales.
The aquarium says it does not know if the deaths are related, but they are performing tests and necropsies.

articles.title: Jinggoy Estrada enters 'not guilty' plea in flood control-related plunder, graft charges
articles.summary: Sen. Jinggoy Estrada refused to enter a plea for his graft and plunder charges before the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Thursday, September 3.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 10:46am
Sen.Jinggoy Estrada leaves the Sandiganbayan in Quezon City after attending his scheduled arraignment on the graft case filed against him at the Sandiganbayan in Quezon City on June 2, 2026.
STAR / Miguel de Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Jinggoy Estrada refused to enter a plea for his graft and plunder charges before the Sandiganbayan Fifth Division on Thursday, September 3.
A "not guilty" plea was automatically entered on his behalf during his arraignment today.
Estrada is facing graft and plunder charges in connection to the alleged kickback scheme that led to irregularities in flood control works.
He is accused of receiving P573.75 million in kickbacks through the manipulation and rigging of processes and siphoning funds from the flood control budget.

Former Department of Public Works and Highways Secretary Manuel Bonoan, originally charged alongside Estrada, has seen his charges dropped following a motion from the Ombudsman to have him be a state witness instead.
Estrada is currently detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas and has been suspended from his work as senator.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says Iran attacked vessel in Hormuz, killing 2 Filipino sailors
articles.summary: The oil tanker Sidr, owned by Bahri, was one of two supertankers carrying Saudi oil reported to have been hit late on August 31 while transiting the Strait of Hormuz

blocks.text: HORMUZ. Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz, as seen from Musandam, Oman, July 9, 2026
The oil tanker Sidr, owned by Bahri, was one of two supertankers carrying Saudi oil reported to have been hit late on August 31 while transiting the Strait of Hormuz
Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, said on Wednesday, September 2, that an Iranian attack on an oil tanker owned by its national shipping company had killed two Filipino seafarers.
Sidr, owned by Bahri, was one of two supertankers carrying Saudi oil reported to have been hit late on Monday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has threatened tankers attempting to sail through the narrow waterway without authorisation, impeding energy exports from neighboring oil-rich Gulf countries.
About one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade used to pass through the Strait of Hormuz before the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.
Bahri said the seafarers were killed in a security incident involving Sidr at 23:40 local time (2040 GMT) on Monday.
“The kingdom stressed the necessity of halting escalations, and respecting international maritime safety and the security of global energy supplies,” the Saudi foreign ministry said.

“Bahri remains in continuous contact with the vessel and is coordinating closely with the relevant authorities and maritime industry stakeholders, while continuing to closely monitor developments,” the company said in a statement.
In July, another Bahri vessel, the Wedyan supertanker, was hit while passing through the strait close to Oman’s coast.
Two other Bahri vessels, Masa and Amzan, were attacked in the Red Sea in July and August after the Iran-backed Yemen’s Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Two Filipino seafarers killed as Saudi tanker attacked in Hormuz
articles.summary: Fourteen other Filipino crew members aboard tanker Sidr are safe.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 10:33am
The Strait of Hormuz as seen in this 2026 satellite imagery from NASA via Google Maps.
Philstar.com screenshot

MANILA, Philippines — Two Filipino seafarers were killed after the Saudi-flagged crude oil tanker Sidr was struck by unidentified projectiles while approaching the Strait of Hormuz, the Department of Migrant Workers confirmed.
At an online briefing on Wednesday, September 2, Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said 16 Filipino seafarers were aboard the vessel when it was attacked late Aug. 31.
The strike caused a fire that the crew managed to contain, but two of the Filipino seafarers died.
The remains of the two victims have been taken to Oman, while the 14 surviving Filipino crew members are safe and being prepared for repatriation.
Cacdac said the Philippine Embassy and Migrant Workers Office in Oman are coordinating with Omani authorities to bring the crew members and the remains of those killed back to the Philippines.

Saudi national shipping company Bahri, which operates the Sidr, separately confirmed that two Filipino seafarers were killed in a "security incident" involving the tanker at around 11:40 p.m. local time on August 31.
High-risk waterway
The attack comes amid renewed fighting between the United States and Iran around the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important energy shipping routes.

The United States struck Iranian missile launchers on Larak Island over the weekend, prompting Iran to retaliate against U.S. bases in Jordan. Maritime authorities subsequently reported attacks on commercial vessels transiting the strait.
Saudi Arabia has blamed Iran for the attack on the Sidr. Iran has not publicly accepted responsibility.
Cacdac said 31 vessels carrying 421 Filipino seafarers have been attacked in incidents involving the Strait of Hormuz since Feb. 28.
Of the 421 seafarers, 406 were unharmed, 10 were injured but have since recovered, three were killed and one remains missing. A total of 268 have returned to the Philippines.
Around 3,000 Filipino seafarers are still estimated to be aboard vessels in the wider Persian Gulf, according to the DMW.
Right to refuse
The DMW remains on red alert and has reminded shipowners to conduct risk assessments, put adequate security measures in place and avoid exposing Filipino crews to high-risk waters where possible.
Cacdac also reiterated that Filipino seafarers have the right to refuse to sail into designated high-risk or warlike areas.
"We are disallowing deployment to the extent that a seafarer exercises the right to refuse to sail. That right must be respected," Cacdac said.
The DMW and Bahri said assistance would be extended to the survivors and the families of the two seafarers who died. — with reports from Reuters

blocks.text: OLONGAPO CITY — A 35-year-old father was found dead on Wednesday, a day after he and his seven-year-old son went missing after a carabao-drawn cart he was steering was swept away by strong river currents in Botolan town, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) said.

Simeon Candule, a resident of Barangay Palis in Botolan, was traveling home with his son around 1 p.m. on Tuesday when a strong, fast-flowing current threw them off the cart and into the river, which swept them downstream, according to a Coast Guard report.

An initial search and rescue team was deployed to accessible portions of the riverbank, followed by an intensified surface search where responders spotted a body along the shoreline. A family member positively identified the remains of Candule.
The Coast Guard turned over the body of Candule to his family and transported them to Barangay Palis, while the search for his son continues./coa

articles.title: Australia’s new environmental protection agency approves coal project, angering climate groups
articles.summary: Queensland open-cut Saraji mine will be able to keep digging until 2055 as Anthony Albanese denies tensions with Pacific leaders over fossil fuels

blocks.text: Australia’s new national agency for environmental protection has approved its first coal project, allowing a Queensland open-cut mine to keep digging until 2055 while clearing threatened woodland and koala habitat.

The confirmation of the extension of the Saraji mine, which digs and exports coal for steel making, comes after the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, denied this week there was tension over Australia’s fossil fuel exports during talks with Pacific leaders.
The National Environmental Protection Agency confirmed to Guardian Australia it had approved the BHP Mitsubishi Alliance (BMA) mine extension to dig a further 55m tonnes of coal between now and 2055.
The approval is the agency’s first green light for a coal project since it began operations on 1 July after being created during reforms to national environment laws last year.

An agency spokesperson said the approval came with “strict conditions to protect threatened species and water resources” and would limit clearing of habitat for threatened koalas, ornamental snakes and squatter pigeons.

In its application, BMA said it would likely have to clear 9.7 hectares of endangered koala habitat, 14.2 hectares of vulnerable ornamental snake habitat, 39 hectares of habitat of the vulnerable squatter pigeon and 3.1 hectares of threatened Brigalow woodland.
The agency’s approval said the company must not clear more than 132.5 hectares of ornamental snake habitat, 162 ha of squatter pigeon habitat and 11.5 ha of koala habitat.
At this week’s Pacific Islands Forum, Albanese said the meeting’s “entry fee for credibility” was “taking climate change seriously”.
When asked about fossil fuel expansions, Albanese denied leaders of Pacific nations who fear for their country’s future because of rising sea levels had raised objections.
“No, they don’t do that,” he said.
“Australia is highly regarded when it comes to climate change, and the talking down of Australia does not happen from outside Australia. I’ll make that point.

“The Pacific leaders have respect for the position that we’ve taken, and they also understand with the transition, because they’re dealing with it as well, that the transition can’t happen overnight, that it requires strategies and policies to be put in place.”

Ben McLeod, a senior adviser at the Climate Council, said burning coal overseas to make steel would release about 120m tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere over the life of the mine. Australia’s current annual emissions are 455m tonnes.
after newsletter promotion

“This leaves us incredulous,” said McLeod. “The prime minister said the entry fee for the forum was taking climate change seriously, but then we get this approval of 55 million tonnes of coal. It is hard to see how those two things are compatible.”
He said the approval by the new agency illustrated the government’s reforms to environment laws had not been strong enough in dealing with climate pollution.

He said the climate “does not care” if the emissions from burning coal were to generate electricity or make steel, and pointed to International Energy Agency advice that to meet net zero emissions by 2050 there was no requirement for more coalmines.

Greenpeace Australia Pacific said the Saraji approval was the 37th fossil fuel project approved by the Albanese government, and was a “double talk” and an “affront” to Pacific leaders and communities.

Dr Simon Bradshaw of Greenpeace Australia Pacific said: “It is deeply insincere for prime minister Albanese to meet Pacific leaders here in Palau to discuss security, the energy crisis, and regional threats, while his government fast-tracks the biggest security threat to the Pacific, the climate crisis.

“We are witnessing dangerous climate change driven by the production, export and burning of fossil fuels, wreaking havoc across the world. Continuing down the path of fossil fuels and approving new coal is an act of recklessness at a pivotal moment in the world’s energy transition and response to the climate crisis.”

Dr Carol Rowston, director of the group Environmental Advocacy Central Queensland, said the mine’s extension would put more pressure on threatened species and on water quality in the Fitzroy River catchment during flooding.
Guardian Australia has approached the environment minister, Murray Watt, for comment.

articles.title: Molly Ticehurst’s father tells DV murderer he hopes daughter’s screams will haunt him forever
articles.summary: Tony Ticehurst confronts Daniel Billings during sentence hearing in regional NSW, stating: ‘When she died, part of me died with her’

blocks.text: The family of Molly Ticehurst, who was murdered by her abusive ex-boyfriend Daniel Billings in her home in central western New South Wales in 2024, has come face-to-face with her killer.
Tony Ticehurst on Thursday described his 28-year-old daughter as big-hearted and deeply loved. She was his best friend and confidant, he told the supreme court in Orange.
His voice heavy with emotion, Ticehurst addressed Billings directly several times, describing him as selfish.
“I hope that every night Molly’s screams keep you awake,” Tony Ticehurst told the first day of Billings’ sentence hearing.
“When she died, part of me died with her. I believe that after you serve your punishment here on earth, the justice system of the universe will judge you.”
Molly’s mother, Kate, held her hand tightly over her face as her victim impact statement was read by a relative.
“Molly was my only child and my best friend,” her statement read. “I’m heartbroken that my girl is no longer with me.”
Billings was wearing a black suit and white shirt with sneakers. He often leaned his head against the back of the dock and closed his eyes on Thursday.
He bowed his head while listening to several victim impact statements.
About 50 of Molly’s family and friends attended the hearing, some wearing shirts saying “Her name was Molly”.
The court heard Billings broke into her Forbes bedroom just before midnight on 21 April 2024. He stabbed Molly 15 times in a ferocious attack that lasted less than a minute.
The trainee mining driller had repeatedly threatened to break into her home and kill her in the preceding weeks and months.
He had been charged with several counts of raping Molly and a string of domestic violence offences, but was freed on bail by a local court registrar a fortnight before the murder.
Police had taken out a provisional apprehended violence order against Billings.
Billings pleaded guilty to murder in November 2025 after 18 months of legal negotiations. The sexual assault charges were subsequently dropped.
Molly Ticehurst’s murder intensified a national campaign against gendered violence and led to legal changes in NSW, including tighter bail laws for people accused of domestic violence.

blocks.caption: A court sketch of Daniel Billings in late August. Photograph: Rocco Fazzari/AAP

blocks.text: Her father said that had brought some comfort, along with knowing his daughter was now safe from Billings.
“Molly’s law has now been introduced; I will be forever proud to be her dad,” he told the court.
Donna Thornell, the mother of Orange woman Kristy Armstrong, who was killed when her abusive estranged husband ran her car off a road in 2023, was also in court to support the Ticehursts.
The court was on Thursday viewing several hours of videos that Billings made before the murder, in which he foreshadowed the crime.
Charges of property damage, animal cruelty offences and breaching the apprehended violence order were to be taken into consideration in Billings’ sentence.
Justice Natalie Adams has indicated she will hand down her sentence later in September.

articles.summary: HANOI — Vietnamese police arrested a deputy health minister on Wednesday for allegedly accepting huge bribes, part of a probe into a company accused of smuggling medical equipment, authorities…

blocks.text: HANOI — Vietnamese police arrested a deputy health minister on Wednesday for allegedly accepting huge bribes, part of a probe into a company accused of smuggling medical equipment, authorities said.
Communist Vietnam has pursued a high-profile anti-corruption campaign in recent years that has netted dozens of business leaders and senior government figures.

Deputy Health Minister Tran Van Thuan, a leading oncologist in Vietnam, was taken into custody “due to his acceptance of bribes involving a large sum of money”, the public security ministry said in a statement, without specifying the amount.
Thuan, 56, was appointed deputy health minister in 2020 and chairman of the National Medical Council in 2024.

His arrest came as part of a police investigation involving “smuggling” and “violations of accounting regulations causing serious consequences” at Viet My Medical Investment Joint Stock Company, the ministry’s statement said.

Police have arrested two executives and an accountant at the firm, which was allegedly set up to trade, resell and inflate the prices of medical equipment and pharmaceuticals before importing them from Singapore and Hong Kong into Vietnam, state media said.
Police also accuse company leaders of attempting to illegally import medical equipment.
AFP was unable to contact the company for comment.
Vietnam’s sweeping anti-corruption drive, accelerated by President To Lam, has removed many of his opponents, according to analysts, leaving him as the country’s most dominant leader in decades.
In May, former health minister Nguyen Thi Kim Tien was imprisoned for six years over her mismanagement of hospital projects, state media said.
Tien was rocked by corruption scandals in previous years, and was once voted the least popular official by lawmakers in the one-party state. /dl

articles.summary: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Four centenarians in this city each received P50,000 in cash incentives and food packs from the Bukidnon provincial government on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, bringing the…

blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Four centenarians in this city each received P50,000 in cash incentives and food packs from the Bukidnon provincial government on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, bringing the total number of registered provincial centenarian-beneficiaries to 56.

Gov. Rogelio Neil Roque handed the cash assistance and food packs to Julia Lacre, 100, of Kibalaan, Barangay Guinuyoran; Carmellina Villas (101) of Barangay Sugod; Patricia Sanjurjo, 103, of Barangay Batangan; and Alejandro Maghinay, 106, of Barangay Mabuhay.
Ellen Salumintao, Provincial Social Welfare and Development (PSWD) officer, said 34 of the 56 registered centenarians are currently living in the province.

The registry recorded 31 centenarians in 2024, 16 in 2025, and nine additions in 2026, with five individuals aged 106—three females and two males—currently recorded as Bukidnon’s oldest living centenarians.

Roque stated that the high number of centenarians reflects “Bukidnon’s healthy environment and living conditions,” adding that the provincial government is happy to reciprocate the years of service these senior citizens have rendered to the community.
The local cash incentive is institutionalized under Provincial Ordinance No. 2022-010R, enacted by the 27th Sangguniang Panlalawigan.
The provincial grant provides additional incentives and is separate from the P100,000 cash incentive granted by the national government under the Centenarians Act. /jpv

articles.title: August operations net 286 fugitives in Northern Mindanao
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — A month-long dragnet operation across Northern Mindanao led to the arrest of 286 fugitives in August, including dozens of high-profile suspects who had long been hunted by…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — A month-long dragnet operation across Northern Mindanao led to the arrest of 286 fugitives in August, including dozens of high-profile suspects who had long been hunted by authorities.

Data from the Police Regional Office 10 (PRO-10) showed that of the total arrests made between Aug. 1 and 31, 2026, 72 were tagged as “Most Wanted Persons” (MWPs), while 214 fell under the category of other wanted persons.
Among the top-tier suspects arrested, 10 were listed at the regional level, 36 at the provincial and city levels, and 26 at the municipal level.

Bukidnon accounted for the largest share of the haul with 84 arrests, followed by Misamis Oriental with 49, Cagayan de Oro City with 44, and Misamis Occidental with 41. Rounding out the regional tally were Iligan City with 37, Lanao del Norte with 27, and Camiguin with four.

Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr., PRO-10 director, said the operations were carried out under the directives of the leaderships of the Philippine National Police and the Department of the Interior and Local Government, which prioritize the service of warrants on high-profile fugitives.

“There will be no let-up in our manhunt operations,” Babagay said, pointing out that police units will maximize intelligence resources and strengthen coordination while keeping all operations within legal bounds. /jpv

articles.title: Pangasinan will do dredging to reduce floods, says governor
articles.summary: CALASIAO, Pangasinan – Pangasinan Gov. Ramon Guico III on Wednesday (September 2) said the provincial government is pushing for the dredging of major rivers, most of which have become heavily silted,…

blocks.text: CALASIAO, Pangasinan – Pangasinan Gov. Ramon Guico III on Wednesday (September 2) said the provincial government is pushing for the dredging of major rivers, most of which have become heavily silted, to reduce or eliminate Pangasinan’s seasonal struggles with widespread floods.
“We are going for dredging,” he told the Inquirer in telephone interview.
Guico stressed the need for well-planned and high-quality river protection and infrastructure projects that would address flooding in the long term.
“We should have well thought out and quality river protection and infrastructure projects—a multi-year contract and not a piecemeal approach,” Guico said.

“There must be a study of all major rivers and tributaries in Pangasinan to determine the flow of water,” he added. “Government agencies such as the Departments of Environment and Natural Resources and of Public Works and Highways should conduct these studies so that a feasible river restoration project can be implemented.”
The provincial government has started dredging the Limahong Channel in Lingayen, one of the deltas of the Agno River. The other delta is located in Labrador town.

The project has been contracted out to a private company at no cost to the provincial government, with the company retaining ownership of the materials dredged from the river, because the provincial government has no funds for dredging northward, Guico said.
However, Guico said the effects of the project have yet to be felt because the contractor has only recently begun removing silt from the mouth of the channel.
The company just dredged the entrance of Limahong so the dredging equipment could enter the channel,” he said.
Guico also dismissed reports claiming that solar farms established in the mountainous areas of Pangasinan have contributed to the province’s massive flooding.

He said the areas where the solar farms were established had already lost much of their vegetation even before the projects were put up. While reforestation efforts have been undertaken, he said some of the newly planted trees have been destroyed by fires.

Guico said the provincial government is also coordinating with Dagupan City officials on the possible dredging of the Sabangan River, the delta of the Sinucalan-Marusay-Pantal River system, located between Dagupan City and Binmaley and leading toward the Lingayen Gulf.
Sabangan River is a critical downstream bottleneck, slowing the flow of floodwaters from neighboring towns like Calasiao and Binmaley out toward the Lingayen Gulf.
Guico also pointed out the need to clear the waterways of fish pens as these block the flow of water specially during monsoon season.
Guico also said that while the provincial government has already begun dredging the Marusay River, the effort could be undermined if the Sabangan River remains heavily silted.
“If Sabangan is heavily silted, floodwater will be trapped in the river system because it cannot freely flow toward the Lingayen Gulf,” he said.

The provincial government is likewise preparing to undertake the dredging of the Nayum River, a natural waterway that marks the geographic boundary between Infanta town in Pangasinan, and Santa Cruz town in Zambales.

At of presstime, at least 15 towns and two cities have barangays that are under water, with most still not passable by light vehicles, according to the Pangasinan Provincial Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office.
The municipalities of Mangatarem and Calasiao and Dagupan City still have national roads that are not passable by light vehicles, said Pia Navata Flores, spokesperson of the PDRRMO.
The other towns with flooded barangays for weeks now are Agno, Mabini, Aguilar, Binmaley, Bugallon, Lingayen, Malasiqui, Sta. Barbara, San Jacinto, and Basista as well as San Carlos City.
Basista was the latest to confront floods because of the swelling of the Camiling River.

In Calasiao, all 24 barangays experienced flooding, but five barangays are under about four feet high of floods, said Kristine Joy Soriano, spokesperson of the Municipal Disaster Risk Reduction and Management.
As of 5 am of Wednesday, 3,256 families (10,654 individuals) are still inside evacuation centers in different towns. /jpv

With the US threatening further strikes, Iran accused Washington of hitting a wedding party, killing four people and wounding dozens. Its health minister later said 18 people in total had been killed and 108 injured in the latest wave of US strikes.

The US military said it struck air defenses, radar systems, maritime assets, mine-laying capabilities and communications sites on Tuesday, September 1, Iran reported hits on multiple targets near the Strait of Hormuz.

blocks.caption: US launches new strikes on Iran as Tehran hits back in widening conflict

blocks.text: The flare-up threatens to deepen a conflict that has dragged on since the US launched strikes on Iran in February, disrupting global energy supplies and drawing opposition from a majority of Americans ahead of November’s congressional elections.

“Last night was like the end of the world,” Mahmoud, 38, a municipal worker in Sirik County along the strait, told Reuters by telephone, describing attacks on the area that includes the city where the wedding was reported to have been hit.
President Donald Trump said the US hit Iran “very hard” and that Iran only responded with a “love tap.”
“It was a very heavy attack last night, and we’re prepared to do another one any time we want,” Trump told reporters at the White House.

Iran struck what it said were US assets in Bahrain, Jordan, Kuwait and Iraq, and said its aim was now to drive US forces from the vast network of military bases they have maintained for decades across the Middle East.

“American evil in the region will be met with heavier, more widespread, and devastating responses, and any country that cooperates with the aggressive American army must accept its dangerous consequences,” Iran’s military command said.
Iran said it killed US forces in Jordan and at a base in northern Iraq, but US officials told Reuters there had not been any casualties, according to initial assessments.

In Kuwait, Iran said it had carried out a missile and drone attack on the US Ali Al Salem air base and on a residential complex used by a US commander. Kuwait’s fire service said it put out a blaze at a residential complex hit by a drone.

Qatar, home of the largest US air base in the Gulf, said it held Iran responsible for attacks and their repercussions. Bahrain, which houses the regional headquarters of the US Navy, said Iranian drones were intercepted and destroyed.
Iran also said two tankers had been struck by mines while being steered through the Strait of Hormuz by US personnel.
Washington says that despite Iranian attacks it is guiding ships through the strait. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said more than 17 million barrels of oil exited on Monday.

Iran blacklisted 11 more ships, bringing the total number of such vessels to 56, a government website showed, meaning it would consider them subject to fines, confiscation or detention if they try to sail through the Strait of Hormuz without Tehran’s permission.
Trump repeated his assertion that the strait, which handled 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments before the war, was open to shipping.
Iranians were fearful that the new strikes signalled war could restart at full scale.
“It’s very difficult to live like this. We don’t know when America will strike,” Mahpari, 28, a woman in the southern port city of Bandar Abbas, told Reuters by phone.

Iran said four people including a 4-year-old were killed while celebrating a wedding at a home in Sirik. Iranian media said as many as 68 people were wounded there, and released images of injured children in hospital.
Reuters was unable to independently verify the incident.

US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins, a spokesperson for Central Command, said: “We are aware of reports, which originated from Iranian state media. The US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC,” referring to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards.
Video shot by Iran’s West Asia News Agency at the purported site showed rubble strewn across rooms and a courtyard. A pair of strappy women’s dress sandals lay abandoned on a blood-soaked carpet.
“I am just glad the casualties weren’t even worse,” said Ali Molahi, identified as the father of the bride.

The exchange of fire was the worst since July, when Trump abruptly halted two weeks of intense bombing of Iran after warnings from his military brass that they were using up munitions and running out of meaningful targets.

Trump has yet to achieve the aims he set when launching “Operation Epic Fury” in February – to end Iran’s nuclear programme, deprive it of the ability to strike its neighbors and create conditions for Iranians to topple their rulers.
But the US has seriously degraded Iran’s conventional military forces and taken a toll on Iran’s already weakening economy, US officials say.

Sources have told Reuters Trump aides are trying to keep the war quiet for now to avert a defeat in the midterm elections in November. Polls show Americans oppose the war by more than a two-to-one margin. – Rappler.com

articles.title: NLEX traffic at Tulaoc portion remains slow-moving amid San Simon floods
articles.summary: NLEX traffic at Tulaoc portion remains slow-moving amid San Simon floods

blocks.text: Published September 3, 2026 8:35am
Traffic along the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) remained slow-moving in the Tulaoc portion amid the flooding in San Simon, Pampanga Thursday morning, according to an official on the toll highway.
NLEX Assistant Vice President for Traffic Operations Robin Ignacio said two lanes under the San Simon Interchange and Tulaoc were already passable despite the flooding.

“Sa ating northbound, nandoon po sa more than one kilometer paatras po ng Tulaoc. And then yung southbound, halos wala na po ito, halos wala na tayong queuing,” he told GMA News’ Unang Balita in an interview.
(On our northbound, the slow-moving traffic was more than one kilometer back from Tulaoc. And then on the southbound, it’s almost gone, we almost don’t have any queuing.)
Floodwaters in Tulaoc already nearly subsided, while around four inches of floodwaters remained in the inner lane at the San Simon Interchange, Ignacio said.
As of 6:50 a.m., the NLEX Corporation said in advisory that the Tulaoc portion had slow-moving traffic in the northbound direction with a queue of approximately 1.5 kilometers.
Lane 1 was passable to all types of vehicles, while Lane 2 was limited to Class 2 and 3 vehicles. Lane 3 was not passable.
At the San Simon Interchange, traffic remained light despite water buildup in all lanes.
In the southbound direction, Tulaoc also had floodwaters across all lanes.
Lanes 1 and 2 were passable to all types of vehicles, while Lane 3 was not passable. Traffic was reported as light.
At the San Simon Interchange southbound, Lane 1 was passable to all types of vehicles, while Lane 2 was limited to Class 2 and 3 vehicles. Lane 3 was not passable.

Meanwhile, several northbound entry points were under traffic restrictions. The Libsong Exit was temporarily closed, while the Sta. Rita, Balagtas, and Pulilan northbound entries were under regulated traffic.

Motorists coming from the Tarlac portion of the Tarlac-Pangasinan-La Union Expressway (TPLEX) or Subic-Clark-Tarlac Expressway (SCTEX) and heading south were advised to take the Central Luzon Link Expressway (CLLEX) toward Maharlika Highway.
Ignacio said clearing the floodwater remained challenging because water levels outside the expressway were higher.
NLEX had installed temporary flood barriers including sandbags to prevent additional water from entering the expressway.

The company also distributed drinking water and deployed portable toilets for motorists affected by the traffic. Ignacio, however, said the influx of vehicles increased after other alternate routes were flooded.
Ignacio said the flooding under the San Simon Interchange was unprecedented as the area had not experienced flooding before.
The Tulaoc section had already been raised by 0.7 meter but further elevation is being considered, according to the NLEX official.
He noted that this additional action needs to be coordinated with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) as the agency plans to raise the bridge above the affected section.

Ignacio said continuously raising the road may not be enough to address the worsening flooding. There is a proposal to establish a large water impounding area nearby where floodwaters could temporarily be stored and later pumped out once water levels subside.

Motorists using the affected NLEX stretch between Pulilan and San Fernando will receive a toll rebate while traffic remains disrupted. The toll fee for the affected section will be credited back to motorists' RFID accounts within 24 hours.
Ignacio said the toll rebate would continue until traffic flow in the affected section returns to normal. —VAL, GMA News

blocks.text: BAGUIO City— Burnham Park’s boat concessionaires were given a final warning on Wednesday, over charging excessive rental rates, a day after its newly renovated man-made lake was reopened to the public following a year of repairs.

The city government threatened to revoke their licenses to operate at the lake if boat rental owners fail to comply with government-set rates, upgrade their boats and issue official receipts to customers.
City Administrator Vittorio Jericho Cawis issued the ultimatum during a Wednesday meeting called by lawyer Rhenan Diwas, the City Environment and Parks Management Officer.
“This is the final warning. If they continue not to comply, then we will be compelled to open their slots to other residents wishing to apply as boating concessionaires,” Cawis said.

The concessionaires were directed to charge the existing rate of P250 per boat for 30 minute rides around the 4-hectare lake. Many residents who hired boats on Tuesday, a holiday to commemorate Baguio’s 117th Charter Day, were aghast when charged for as much as P400.
Boats that have not been upgraded will also not be allowed to operate for public use starting Sept. 2, the city government said. /dp

articles.title: Rare train of Pacific cyclones fueled by historic El Niño
articles.summary: WASHINGTON — Two powerful hurricanes and a strengthening tropical storm on Wednesday were churning through the Pacific Ocean where waters were being warmed by a historically strong El Niño…

blocks.text: WASHINGTON — Two powerful hurricanes and a strengthening tropical storm on Wednesday were churning through the Pacific Ocean where waters were being warmed by a historically strong El Niño climate episode.

Furthest west is Hurricane Lowell, followed by Hurricane Karina. Both of the Category 4 storms are anticipated to pass well to the south and to the northeast of Hawaii, respectively, according to the National Hurricane Center (NHC).
However, uncertainty remains over their tracks, with the possibility Lowell could pass close to the archipelago’s westernmost islands.
Hawaii is still recovering from the impacts of Hurricane Lala, which brushed past the southern part of the Big Island last month, bringing destructive winds and severe flash floods.
Lowell and Karina are trailed to the east by Tropical Storm Marie, currently a few hundred miles south of Baja California and “expected to become a hurricane later today,” the NHC said.

“El Niño warming sets the stage for these storms, which are fueled in large part by warm waters — when the tropical Pacific is warmer than normal we see an increase in strong storms,” Julia Cole, a climate scientist at the University of Michigan, told AFP.
A train of three cyclones “is definitely rare to see,” she added.
A similar train of four cyclones happened in 2015, another intense El Niño year, when Typhoon Kilo, Hurricane Ignacio, Hurricane Jimena and Tropical Depression 14E crossed the Pacific at once.
“The climate system has significantly warmed over the last 20 years or so,” said Benjamin Kirtman, an atmospheric scientist at the University of Miami.
Warm waters provide fuel for storms, and El Niño’s effect on the atmosphere leaves little vertical wind shear over the Pacific, creating favorable conditions for hurricanes to intensify.
“There’s no other way to put it — it is juicy out there right now,” he told AFP.

What’s more, the sea surface temperature anomaly — how much warmer the ocean is compared to average — is already near record high, right in the middle of the Pacific hurricane season, Kirtman explained.
Impacts felt worldwide

This year’s El Niño has a 69 percent chance of becoming the strongest on record, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and is already unleashing extreme weather across the globe even though it is not expected to peak until October-December.

Peru, the world’s largest catcher of anchovy, is facing a devastating blow from warming seas that have gutted production, according to industry officials. In Sudan, El Niño is blamed for delaying crucial rains that have led water levels in the Nile to drop precipitously.
El Niño is the warming phase of a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific known as the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), and comes along every two to seven years.
It sets in when east-to-west trade winds ease, allowing warm water which normally piles up in the western Pacific Ocean to slide back east and rise to the surface.

When those warmer-than-average surface temperatures last for a few months, they cause more storms and clouds over the region, which in turn cause ripple effects through the entire global atmosphere: hotter and drier conditions in some places, cooler and wetter in others.

Climate change increases El Niño’s impacts. A warmer atmosphere holds more moisture, so El Niño-linked rains can turn more extreme. It also dries out soils, deepening drought where El Niño brings drought. /dl

articles.title: [Ask the Tax Whiz] Clarifying some tax issues related to ONETT transactions
articles.summary: ONETT refers to transactions that are subject to one-time tax compliance and processing with the BIR

blocks.text: ONETT refers to transactions that are subject to one-time tax compliance and processing with the BIR

items: One-Time Transactions (ONETT) include the sale of real property, transfer of shares, donations, and estate property transfers, all requiring tax compliance and BIR documentation.
The BIR can issue the Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR) even if the Value-Added Tax (VAT) is unpaid, but this does not absolve the taxpayer of their VAT obligations.
Tax classification for properties is based on the Tax Declaration rather than actual use, affecting the applicable taxes such as Capital Gains Tax and Documentary Stamp Tax.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
The Philippine Tax Whiz answers common questions on ONETT transactions and explains key tax issues clarified by the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) under Revenue Memorandum Circular No. 75-2026.
ONETT refers to transactions that are subject to one-time tax compliance and processing with the BIR. These include the following:

items: Sale of real property classified as a capital asset;
Sale, transfer, or assignment of shares of stock not traded through the stock exchange;
Sale of real property classified as an ordinary asset;
Donation of property; and
Transfer of properties arising from a decedent’s estate.

blocks.text: Taxpayers undertaking any of these transactions are generally required to comply with the applicable documentary requirements, pay the corresponding taxes, and secure the necessary BIR-issued documents, such as the Electronic Certificate Authorizing Registration (eCAR), before the property or shares can be validly transferred or registered.

Yes. The BIR may still issue the eCAR even if the VAT due on the transaction has not yet been paid. However, the issuance of the eCAR does not extinguish the taxpayer’s obligation to pay the applicable VAT. The concerned office issuing the eCAR shall inform the Revenue District Office (RDO) for the appropriate assessment and collection of the VAT due, if applicable.

Accordingly, taxpayers should not interpret the issuance of the eCAR as confirmation that all tax liabilities arising from the transaction have been fully settled. Any unpaid VAT remains subject to assessment and collection by the concerned RDO.
No. The computation shall be whichever is highest of the following amounts:

items: Selling Price (as shown on Deed of Absolute Sale or DOAS, excluding Capital Gains Tax)
Fair Market Value (FMV) or Zonal Value determined by the BIR commissioner

FMV by the Provincial or City Assessor until amended by the Real Property Valuation and Assessment Reform Act (RPVARA), where it is based on Schedule of Market Value (SMV) or actual gross selling price, whichever is higher.

blocks.text: The Documentary Stamp Tax (DST) shall likewise be computed the same as the basis of CGT, except in government transactions, where DST is based on the consideration paid.

Yes. A dacion en pago is considered a transfer of ownership where a debtor conveys property to a creditor as settlement of an existing obligation. Although the transaction is intended to settle a debt, it is treated as a transfer of property for tax purposes.
The applicable taxes depend on the classification of the property transferred:

items: If the property is classified as a capital asset: Capital Gains Tax (CGT) Documentary Stamp Tax (DST)
If the property is classified as an ordinary asset: Creditable Withholding Tax (CWT) Value-Added Tax (VAT), if applicable Documentary Stamp Tax (DST)

blocks.caption: When is a deed of sale considered antedated, graphic, ask the tax whiz, asian consulting group, dacion en pago

blocks.text: No. For purposes of computing the applicable taxes, the classification indicated in the Tax Declaration shall be the basis, and not merely the actual use of the property.

For instance, a property may be currently used as a small bake shop or other commercial establishment; however, if the Tax Declaration classifies the property as residential, such classification shall be considered in determining the applicable tax treatment.

Similarly, a property with an area of less than 1,000 square meters that is classified as agricultural in the Tax Declaration shall not be automatically considered residential solely because of its size. The classification reflected in the Tax Declaration shall prevail in determining the applicable tax treatment. – Rappler.com

articles.title: UNICEF: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse
articles.summary: A survey of around 21,000 young people by the UN's agency for children has found that online sexual abuse of minors is on the rise.

image.caption: A new survey by UNICEF found that one in five teenagers had been the target of online sexual abuse over the past yearImage: Robin Utrecht/ROBIN UTRECHT/picture alliance

blocks.text: The internet is not a safe place for unsupervised children and young people — by now, that's common knowledge.

Social media platforms are adept at tweaking their algorithms to ensure users of any age remain on their sites. To do that, they often disseminate content that can be dangerous and upsetting for young people.

Studies regularly find a connection between what's known as doomscrolling and a higher risk of psychological problems in the young, including suicidal thoughts. And some of the latest trends in video creation on platforms like TikTok directly endanger the safety of users.
In the United States, Meta, which owns both Instagram and Facebook, recently opted to settle a case against it out of court. A number of US states had claimed that the two platforms harmed children.

blocks.caption: In the court case against Meta, held in Oakland, California, the corporation avoided a conviction by reaching a financial settlement with statesImage: Vicki Behringer/REUTERS

blocks.text: Meta agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion (€14.7 billion) to the states involved and to limit teenagers' access to its platforms to just two hours a day. During the night, access will be completely blocked.

A new survey by UNICEF, the UN agency for children, puts the spotlight on another danger that young people constantly face in the digital world: sexual assault, a threat experienced by one in five people between the ages of 12 and 17 over the past year.
What are the key findings?
The UNICEF report, which DW saw in advance of publication, explains how such attacks often happen.
"It often begins without warning," the authors of the study wrote. "Conversation becomes coercion, and coercion becomes entrapment."

The survey found that more than 15 million children had been exposed to unwanted sexual content. An estimated 9 million were pressured into sexual conversations or asked to share sexual images, while some 4 million had sexual images shared without their consent. The report's authors, however, warn that the true scale is likely far higher.

"The report reveals a painful reality," said UNICEF Executive Director Catherine Russell. "These experiences cause profound emotional and mental distress. Many children suffer in silence, unsure where to turn for help."

Often, the perpetrator of the assault puts pressure on a victim. The victims then feel ashamed and this makes it difficult to tell anybody about what has happened. Of those surveyed, 41% had never told anybody about their assault. Others said they had first confided in friends, siblings or their mothers. Fewer than 1% were reported to authorities.

The stereotype many have of a complete stranger harassing young people online actually only applies in 16% of cases. Most perpetrators — 57% — are already known to their victims. They may be friends, family members or even romantic partners.

In addition, 27% of respondents were not able to identify the people behind the profiles. When perpetrators are known, they include adults but also minors. In many cases, attacks take place in real life as well as online.

The major social media platforms are also the main gateways for this kind of behavior. The UNICEF report says 60% of assaults come primarily from Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram (all of which are owned by Meta), followed by Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube. And 14% of respondents cited online gaming platforms as the location of an assault — gaming platforms usually have direct messaging channels.
How was the data collected?

The report polled around 21,000 young people in 21 countries, aged between 12 and 17, who regularly use the internet. Data from 12 countries — Ethiopia, Indonesia, Cambodia, Kenya, Malaysia, Mozambique, Namibia, the Philippines, Tanzania, Thailand, Uganda and Vietnam — had already been collected in 2020 and 2021 and analyzed in an earlier report.

For this new report, additional data was collected in Armenia, Brazil, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Mexico, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Pakistan and Serbia. The surveys were also supplemented by longer interviews with 100 young people who had experienced abuse.

blocks.caption: Children and young people also come into contact with inappropriate content in the form of fakes created by generative AI, such as these images generated by Grok of the platform XImage: Leon Neal/Getty Images

blocks.text: Europe, US surveys find similar results
Researchers familiar with this issue would not be surprised by the scale of the problem.
The 2020 EU Kids Online Survey, based on a poll conducted in 19 European countries, indicated that 22% of all participants had received sexually explicit messages online.

In a Spanish study conducted in seven secondary schools in 2021 and 2022, 21% of female respondents said they were sexually harassed online "occasionally," while 5% said this happened "frequently." For male respondents in the Spanish study, the percentages were a few points lower.

A similar survey conducted by the Pew Research Center in 2022 found that 17% of 13- to 17-year-olds in the US said they had been sent explicit images without their consent. The survey did not differentiate between sexually explicit content and other material that showed things like violence.
Social media bans in Australia, UK, France
The UNICEF report calls on governments, tech companies and other stakeholders to better protect children and young people in the digital world.
Among the requests:

items: Design more secure digital platforms, with stronger protection for the privacy of minors.
Strengthen national regulations and criminal law, and close loopholes.
Establish trustworthy reporting and support systems for young people.

blocks.text: Coming just after Meta's out-of-court settlement in the US, the new UNICEF report will likely add fuel to the fire for those seeking to ban social media for young people, an ongoing debate in many countries.

In December 2025, Australia became the first country in the world to introduce an age limit for social media in order to protect minors. There, anyone under 16 is prohibited from having an account on platforms like YouTube, X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat, a rule the platforms themselves are required to monitor.

A similar age limit will come into effect in the UK in 2027, while France is the first EU country to have passed a law adopting an age limit — 15 years old — for social media users. However, it has since been blocked by France's top court, the Constitutional Council, which ruled it might infringe on freedom of expression and privacy.
In June, a German commission proposed a tiered model. This would come with age limits, requirements for proof of age and strict rules requiring the cooperation of social media platforms.
This article was originally written in German.
