articles.title: Sea turtle hatchling released in Batanes
articles.summary: ROXAS, Isabela – A sea turtle hatchling had been released along the coast of Ivana town in the island province of Batanes, the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (PENRO) said on…

blocks.text: ROXAS, Isabela – A sea turtle hatchling had been released along the coast of Ivana town in the island province of Batanes, the Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Office (PENRO) said on Tuesday (September 1).

The hatchling’s release was part of its ongoing program for the conservation and protection of sea turtles and their natural habitat, said Victoria Baliuag, Batanes provincial environment and natural resources officer.

The conservation and development section of the Department of Environment and Natural Resources has been surveilling turtle nests and oversees the safe release of the hatched sea turtles to ensure their smooth journey from the nest to the ocean, she said.
The PENRO also discovered another sea turtle nest in the same area on June 11. It was immediately secured with a net to protect the eggs from predators and other possible threats.
Continuous monitoring and protection of sea turtle nesting sites are important ways to ensure the safety of the eggs until they hatch, Baliuag said.
She encouraged local communities to cooperate in the conservation and protection of sea turtles and other wildlife. Other turtle nesting sites may lie in the area. /jpv

articles.title: Baguio, Benguet cancel classes Thursday due to bad weather
articles.summary: BAGUIO CITY — Face-to-face classes from preschool to Grade 12 in Baguio City and Benguet province have been suspended on Thursday, as heavy rains and strong wind pound their communities. Acting…

blocks.text: BAGUIO CITY — Face-to-face classes from preschool to Grade 12 in Baguio City and Benguet province have been suspended on Thursday, as heavy rains and strong wind pound their communities.
Acting Baguio City Mayor Faustino Olowan announced the suspension in anticipation of poor weather conditions that have affected the mountain city for weeks.
Olowan said authorities would issue further announcements on early Thursday morning depending on the prevailing weather and local conditions.

In Benguet, Governor Melchor Diclas ordered the suspension of face-to-face classes from preschool to senior high school, including classes for Alternative Learning System (ALS) enrollees, in both public and private schools across the province through Executive Order No. 2026-68.
Schools were encouraged to implement appropriate learning continuity measures to make up for the disruption.
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) placed Baguio City and Benguet under a yellow rainfall warning until the afternoon of Sept. 3. /dp

articles.title: Classes in 2 Zambales towns, Olongapo suspended amid habagat rains
articles.summary: OLONGAPO City — Classes at all levels in both public and private schools in two Zambales towns were suspended again on Thursday, Sept. 3, due to the continuing inclement weather. The local…

blocks.text: OLONGAPO City — Classes at all levels in both public and private schools in two Zambales towns were suspended again on Thursday, Sept. 3, due to the continuing inclement weather.

The local governments of Subic and Castillejos announced the cancellation of classes, a day after some Zambales municipalities had resumed classes following a brief respite from lashing monsoon rains.
In Olongapo, face-to-face classes in all levels in both public and private schools will also remain suspended on Thursday.
Mayor Rolen Paulino Jr. said schools would shift to alternative learning protocols while the suspension remains in effect.

“Asahan po sa mga susunod na araw na magiging mas localized ang suspension ng mga pasok. Kukunsulta po tayo sa mga school heads ng mga public at private school para sa pinakabalanseng pagsuspend ng pasok,” Paulino said in his announcement

(Expect class suspensions to become more localized in the coming days. We will consult with the school heads of public and private schools to determine the most balanced approach to suspending classes)

Classes in the city have been suspended since Wednesday (September 2) despite slightly improved weather conditions to allow schools and communities to conduct cleanup operations following recent flooding.

The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said Zambales could receive 50 to 100 millimeters of rain due to the southwest monsoon until Saturday, Sept. 5. /dp

articles.title: 12 years after peace deal, violence still stalks Bangsamoro
articles.summary: Upcoming regional elections pose risks of voter intimidation and violence, prompting calls for police reforms, tighter firearm controls, and better military-police coordination to keep the vote…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO, Philippines – The war that once consumed parts of Mindanao has long ended, but the machineries that sustained violence have proved far more difficult to dismantle.

In the Bangsamoro region, the old conflict has given way to a more diffused and persistent disorder, with clan feuds, political rivalries and criminal networks continuing to flourish where the institutions meant to keep the peace remain weak.

Twelve years after a landmark peace agreement, the International Crisis Group said in a report released on Thursday, September 3, that the region’s fragile security system remains heavily dependent on the military.

Weak policing and justice institutions have left soldiers carrying much of the burden of maintaining order in the seven-year-old Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, even as the government seeks to move the military away from counterinsurgency and toward external defense.

The International Crisis Group report was released barely two weeks ahead of the Muslim-majority region’s first regional parliamentary elections since it replaced the now-defunct Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

The 2014 peace agreement between the government during the presidency of the late Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) ended years of fighting, while the BARMM was established in 2019 as part of the transition to peace.

On Tuesday, September 1, Presidential Adviser on Peace, Reconciliation and Unity Mel Senen Sarmiento said the country’s focus had “decisively shifted” from navigating the challenges of internal conflict toward peacebuilding, adding that “the dividends of peace are now upon us.”

Sarmiento said a just and lasting peace required more than “silencing the instruments of war and signing peace accords,” adding that efforts should also focus on nurturing communities where “positive peace can firmly take root and flourish.”

He said the success of the September 14 election would not be measured by who wins or loses, but by whether the Bangsamoro people were able to vote freely, peace was preserved, and the result reflected the genuine choice of the electorate.

The government and MILF peace implementing panels, led by Sarmiento and his counterpart, Mohagher Iqbal, also signed a pledge of commitment for the peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the Bangsamoro elections. (LIVE UPDATES: First BARMM parliamentary elections)

The International Crisis Group report said progress in curbing violence in the BARMM has been uneven, with clan feuds, electoral rivalries, and criminal activities still posing a greater threat than fighting between the state and militant groups.

It said over a third of young people in the region have experienced armed conflict in or near their homes since 2019, based on a 2024 youth assessment. A local conflict watchdog, using data from community networks, recorded hundreds of incidents since January.
The think tank said jihadist groups that stayed outside the peace process remain a security threat, although it noted that attacks on state forces have declined.
It also noted that remnants of the communist New People’s Army operate in parts of Lanao del Sur and Maguindanao del Norte.
Land disputes, rido (clan feuds) and political rivalries remain major sources of violence, with local disputes sometimes escalating into large-scale clashes, the group said.

Easy access to firearms has fueled recurring cycles of violence, it said, while key provisions of the peace agreement, including the disarmament of former rebels and private militias and the redeployment of troops, remain incomplete.

The proliferation of firearms, it said, remains a major source of insecurity, with the police estimating in late 2024 that the region had more than 27,000 unregistered firearms, while a source interviewed by Crisis Group estimated that about 20,000 were legally registered.

Based on the 2014 peace agreement, the MILF has gradually decommissioned its forces. About 14,000 fighters and 2,450 weapons remained to be decommissioned in 2026, underscoring the unfinished nature of the process.

The MILF, however, suspended its formal engagement with the government earlier this year over what it saw as Manila’s failure to fulfill promises of socioeconomic benefits before resuming talks in August. Demobilization, however, appeared to remain on hold.
The region’s illicit economy has changed since the 2014 peace deal. Kidnapping for ransom, once a major problem in Mindanao, has almost disappeared, but smuggling has proliferated, including weapons.
Human trafficking and drug trafficking also remain concerns.

Crisis Group recorded at least 10 anti-drug operations across the predominantly Muslim region since the start of the year. In August, a clash between security forces and an armed drug-trafficking outfit in Tawi-Tawi killed one person and wounded three others, including a naval officer.

The report, “Policing the Bangsamoro: Peace in the Southern Philippines,” said the Philippine National Police had struggled to establish a credible role in parts of the autonomous region affected by violence, while the integration of former Moro rebels into the force had moved slowly.
BARMM communities often view the police as weaker, more politicized, and less dependable than the military, the report said.

The Bangsamoro regional government’s institutions for dispute resolution and justice have also faced challenges, including political infighting, limited resources, and poor access to courts, it added.

Long distances, case backlogs, and high costs have made formal courts difficult to access for many of the region’s poorest residents, while disputes between rival clans can trigger further retaliation even after cases are brought before the justice system.

With the region’s parliamentary elections approaching, rival political blocs and local elites may enlist armed groups to intimidate voters or disrupt the ballot, potentially aggravating tensions in areas where land, political, and clan disputes remain unresolved.

Sarmiento said the government-MILF ceasefire mechanisms must “protect the peace, prevent armed confrontation, address tensions before they escalate, and ensure that our ceasefire mechanisms remain responsive and effective.”

He said the mechanisms “must never be used to favor any candidate, party, or political group,” adding that their “role is not to influence the political choice of the people, but to help create an environment where that choice can be made without fear, coercion, intimidation, or violence.”

Sarmiento urged the Coordinating Committees on the Cessation of Hostilities and the Ad Hoc Joint Action Group to exercise “vigilance and close coordination on the ground” and to “keep communication lines open. Immediately address incidents that may threaten the ceasefire.”
The Crisis Group, meanwhile, called for reforms to professionalize the police, strengthen community policing and improve coordination between the police and military.
It said the military should gradually reduce its role in maintaining public order in areas where security conditions allow, enabling the police to take on more responsibility.
The report also urged tighter controls on firearms, stronger courts, and peacebuilding efforts to address the roots of local conflicts.
“Much as it was a singular achievement to end decades of insurgency, communities will not feel safe until the peace gets the policing it needs,” the report said. – Rappler.com

articles.title: 'Pilandok' set to exit PAR; habagat to continue bringing heavy rains
articles.summary: Tropical Storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) slightly accelerated northwestward over the Philippine Sea and is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Thursday, PAGASA said.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 7:58am

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) slightly accelerated northwestward over the Philippine Sea and is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Thursday, PAGASA said.
In its 5 a.m. bulletin on Thursday, September 3, the state weather bureau said Pilandok was located 1,030 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon as of 4 a.m.
Pilandok was carrying peak winds of 75 kilometers per hour near the center, with gustiness of up to 90 kph and a central pressure of 992 hPa.
It was moving northwestward at 20 kph.
PAGASA said Pilandok is forecast to exit PAR this morning.

Despite the tropical cyclone's departure, the southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to affect parts of the country, bringing heavy rainfall and strong to gale-force winds over several areas through Saturday, September 5.
Strong winds

PAGASA said the southwest monsoon will bring strong to gale-force gusts over most of Luzon and Visayas, as well as Zamboanga del Norte, Misamis Occidental, Lanao del Norte, Misamis Oriental, Camiguin, Dinagat Islands, Davao Occidental and Davao Oriental until Saturday, September 5.
Strong to gale-force gusts are particularly possible in coastal and upland areas exposed to the winds.
Heavy rainfall
The southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to bring heavy rainfall over parts of Luzon and the Visayas through Saturday, September 5, PAGASA said.
Thursday, September 3

items: 50-100 mm: Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro

blocks.text: Friday, September 4

items: 50-100 mm: Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas and Occidental Mindoro

blocks.text: Saturday, September 5

items: 100-200 mm: Occidental Mindoro
50-100 mm: Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga, Cavite, Batangas, Oriental Mindoro and Antique

blocks.text: PAGASA said forecast rainfall may be higher in mountainous and elevated areas.
The state weather bureau also warned that the impacts in some areas may be worsened by significant antecedent rainfall.
Sea conditions
A gale warning is raised over the northern and western seaboards of Northern Luzon.
Very rough seas with waves reaching up to 4.5 meters are expected over the western and southern seaboards of Batanes and the western seaboard of the Babuyan Islands.
Rough seas of up to 4 meters are forecast over the remaining seaboards of Batanes, the northern seaboard of the Babuyan Islands, the seaboards of Ilocos Norte and the northern seaboard of Ilocos Sur.
Waves of up to 3.5 meters are also expected over the remaining seaboard of Ilocos Sur, as well as the seaboards of La Union and Zambales and the western seaboard of Pangasinan.
PAGASA warned that sea travel is risky for all types and tonnage of vessels in areas experiencing very rough seas.
Small seacraft operators, including those using motorbancas, are also advised not to venture out to sea under rough conditions, especially if inexperienced or operating ill-equipped vessels.
Track, intensity
PAGASA said Pilandok is forecast to remain a tropical storm throughout the forecast period.
After exiting PAR, the tropical storm is expected to continue moving generally northwestward toward southern Japan.
Beginning Friday, September 4, until Sunday, September 6, Pilandok is forecast to remain almost stationary before moving generally southward and looping over the Okinawa-Amami islands.
By Monday, September 7, it is expected to move generally southeastward before turning northeastward by Tuesday, September 8.
PAGASA said that heavy rainfall and severe winds may still be experienced in localities outside the forecast confidence cone.
The state weather bureau also said Pilandok's track may still shift within the limit of the forecast confidence cone.

Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand says one of the 30 Canadian citizens and permanent residents missing after catastrophic flooding in Nepal's border region with China has been found safe.
Individual had been unreachable due to communication outages, foreign affairs minister says
She says the individual was unreachable due to communication outages and was able to establish contact Tuesday.
The flash flooding struck one week ago after a glacier collapsed in the Himalayan border region between Nepal and China.
Drone video reveals flood devastation in Devighat, Nepal
More than 1,100 people were killed and more than 3,900 are missing.
Nepal's Foreign Ministry says about 590 foreign nationals from 39 countries remain unaccounted for.
Anand says Canada will be sending more than 18,000 emergency items from Canadian Red Cross stockpiles to the area in addition to the $5 million Ottawa has already pledged in humanitarian aid.

articles.title: Dancing With The Stars announces Season 35 cast: Julia Stiles, Jenna Dewan and more to hit the ballroom floor
articles.summary: The cast of Season 35 of Dancing With The Stars was officially announced on Wednesday, with a fresh lineup of familiar faces trading their famous day jobs for sequins, choreography and a shot at the…

image.caption: The cast of Dancing With The Stars Season 35 includes, from left, Julia Stiles, Harry Shum Jr., Jenna Dewan and Maura Higgins. (Andrew Eccles/Disney)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New

The cast of Season 35 of Dancing With The Stars was officially announced on Wednesday, with a fresh lineup of familiar faces trading their famous day jobs for sequins, choreography and a shot at the mirror-ball trophy.
Hollywood stars, social-media personalities and even a Savannah Banana are stepping onto the dancefloor
The stars have been picked. Now they just need to learn the steps.
Before Wednesday's announcement on Good Morning America, Maura Higgins, Ciara Miller, Jackson Olson and Guillermo Rodriguez had already been confirmed as part of the cast.

Twelve more stars were then named to the roster on the ABC morning show — including Julia Stiles, trading in her Save The Last Dance flats and 10 Things I Hate About You acting chops for the cha-cha-cha, and The Rookie star Jenna Dewan.

With Hollywood heavyweights, social-media personalities, an Olympian, a Paralympian and even a banana stepping onto the dance floor (Savannah Bananas exhibition baseball player Jackson Olson), it's shaping up to be one very busy ballroom.
The show, which airs in Canada on Disney+, will have a double premiere on Sept. 15 and 16.
Here's the full cast and the professional dancers they've been paired with:
Tatyana Ali (Fresh Prince of Bel Air) and Jan Ravnik
Tyler Cameron (The Bachelorette) and Sharna Burgess
Giada De Laurentiis (celebrity chef and Food Network host) and Alan Bersten
Jenna Dewan (The Rookie, Step Up) and Val Chmerkovskiy
Ezra Frech (Paralympian gold medallist) and Daniella Karagach
Amber Glenn (Olympian gold medallist) and Pasha Pashkov
Taylor Hanson (musician) and Britt Stewart
Maura Higgins (Love Island, The Traitors) and Mark Ballas
Conner Leavitt (husband of The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt) and Adele Zaikman
Ciara Miller (Summer House, Love Island USA: Aftersun) and Brandon Armstrong
Sarah Jane Nader (Love Thy Nader) and Hailey Bills
Jackson Olson (Savannah Bananas exhibition baseball player) and Emma Slater
Guillermo Rodriguez (Jimmy Kimmel Live!) and Witney Carson
Harry Shum Jr. (Grey’s Anatomy, Glee and Crazy Rich Asians) and Jenna Chmerkovskiy
Julia Stiles (10 Things I Hate About You, Save The Last Dance) and Ezra Sosa
Connor Wood (comedian, podcaster) and Rylee Arnold
Fans have thoughts
Fans on social media have voiced mixed opinions of the lineup.

That includes casting Dewan, who, unlike many others in the lineup, has an extensive dance background. Before starring in the 2006 dance film Step Up, Dewan worked as a backup dancer for stars including Janet Jackson, Missy Elliott and Christina Aguilera.

Harry Shum Jr., also brings a ton of dance experience to the cast. He's performed alongside major artists like Beyoncé, Mariah Carey, Jennifer Lopez and Madonna, before going on to star in several films in the Step Up franchise.
"That advantage is crazy," one user wrote on X.
"DIABOLICAL. Give someone else a chance 😭," another said.

items: How Dancing with the Stars made all the right moves with Gen Z

blocks.text: But other fans were quick to praise the choice of incoming ballroom competitors, particularly Julia Stiles.
"That’s literally MOTHER. This partnership is going to change lives," one user declared on X. "yeah so this is my team," said another.
A new pro and a family connection

The upcoming season will be the first to feature the winner of Dancing With The Stars: The Next Pro, Adele Zaikman. The competition was hosted by last season's mirror-ball champion and wildlife conservationist Robert Irwin.
This season also marks a big moment for Hailey Bills and the start of a potential fun family feud.
After spending Season 34 as a troupe member on the show, Bills has been promoted to pro and will be part of the third same-sex pairing in Dancing With the Stars history.
Bills is also no stranger to the show’s ballroom — she’s the niece of pro Jenna Johnson, who is married to fellow pro Val Chmerkovskiy.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Griffin Jaeger is a reporter and producer with CBC's entertainment unit. He also formerly hosted and produced content for The National’s digital platforms. You can reach him at griffin.jaeger@cbc.ca

articles.title: Spain: Tens of thousands rally over Ceuta crisis
articles.summary: Tensions continue over migrants still stranded in Ceuta and the Sanchez government’s handling of the fallout.

image.caption: The protests in Madrid and more than 200 other cities and towns were officially organized by the nonpartisan Spanish Federation of Municipalities and ProvincesImage: Violeta Santos Moura/REUTERS

blocks.text: Tens of thousands of people took to the streets across Spain on Wednesday to protest the ongoing border crisis in Ceuta and criticize Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s left-wing government over its handling of the situation.
The protests coincided with Ceuta’s annual official holiday, which is normally marked with celebrations. But this year, the holiday took place against the backdrop of Spain’s ongoing border chaos.
Authorities said around 50,000 people joined the rally in Madrid. Spain’s territorial policy minister, Angel Victor Torres, told Spanish National Radio that the protests were politically motivated.
"This is not to show support for the city of Ceuta or its residents; it is to attack the government of Spain," Torres said.

The government has rejected claims that it has abandoned Ceuta. This week, it allocated €309 million ($357 million) to support the city’s social services, including migrant housing, as well as its security infrastructure.
Police action after rallies to disperse crowds

After the Madrid demonstration ended, an Associated Press journalist reported hearing shots and explosions. Spanish newspaper El Pais reported that police fired rubber bullets and tear gas to disperse crowds.

There were also large turnouts in Barcelona, Valencia and Seville, where demonstrators waved Spanish flags. The protests in Madrid and more than 200 other cities and towns were officially organized by the nonpartisan Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces.

blocks.caption: Protesters rally in Barcelona on September 2, 2026, in support of Ceuta amid the ongoing migration crisis and the arrival of more than 70,000 migrants from MoroccoImage: Lorena Sopêna/Europa Press/IMAGO

blocks.text: The conservative and far-right opposition also used the rallies to attack the government over its handling of the crisis. They accused Sanchez's government on Wednesday of pursuing an appeasement policy towards Morocco.
According to reports, counter-demonstrations were held in some cities where participants spoke out against racism.
One month on, life in Ceuta has yet to return to normal
Many migrants, including unaccompanied minors, remain on the streets and beaches as authorities work to shelter, register and return those eligible to Morocco.
"We’re suffering and we want to get to Europe or find a solution right now," Moroccan migrant Nebil Tazi told The Associated Press. "We’ve been waiting for a month, but there isn’t one."

blocks.caption: Spanish government says most migrants who crossed have since left the enclave but thousands remain wandering the streets and sleeping on beachesImage: Antonio Sempere/AFP

blocks.text: Juan Jesus Vivas, Ceuta’s top official, urged Spain’s central government to reinforce the border with Morocco rather than rely on cooperation with its neighbor. "If we don't do this, there will always be someone tempted to use migration as a tool for political ends," Vivas said.
In a recorded video message published Wednesday, Sanchez said his government was using all available resources to restore tranquility for Ceuta’s residents.

At the end of July, a large number of migrants crossed the border from Morocco into Ceuta, a Spanish North African exclave. Around 5,000 to 8,000 migrants still remain in the territory. The crisis has reignited debate over migration across the EU.

articles.title: Dutch central bank moves 86 tonnes of gold to UK from US and Canada, citing ‘geopolitical unrest’
articles.summary:
Bank says gold reserves held in London could be traded more easily and the move will allow it to respond more rapidly in a ‘crisis situation’

The Dutch central bank says it has moved 86…

blocks.text: The Dutch central bank says it has moved 86 tonnes of its gold reserves out of the US and Canada to London, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest”.
De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) said gold reserves held in London could be traded more easily than those held in New York and Ottawa.
“This makes it the quickest for DNB to deploy in a crisis situation,” the bank said in a statement on Wednesday.

“With this step, we have improved the deployability of the gold reserves. We assume that we will never need to deploy the gold, but it is nevertheless necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness,” said DNB’s president, Olaf Sleijpen.
The total Dutch gold stock amounted to 612.4 tonnes and was valued at €72.2bn ($83.7bn) at the end of 2025, said the DNB.
Before the deployment, the Dutch bank held 31.3% of its gold in New York and 19.7% in Ottawa.
After the move, each country accounted for 18.5% of the Dutch gold reserve.
The share of gold held in London increased from 18.1% to 32.1%. The bank still holds 30.8% of its gold in the Netherlands.
The transfer was carried out partially by buying and selling and partly by physically transferring gold, the bank said.
The bank moved more than 27 tonnes of physical gold from the US and Canada to Zeist.
The same quantity of gold was moved from Zeist to London, preventing the melting down of gold bars.
“By combining buying and selling and physical transport, the risks associated with physically moving a large quantity of gold have been spread,” the DNB said.
The operation took place between March and August of this year, it said.
Laurent Schwartz, president of the Paris-based National Gold Counter, which facilitates gold trading in France, said central banks had been moving their reserves around for about a decade.
“The current political context in the United States might also push certain central banks into favouring other storage locations,” he said.
The London market was the deepest and most liquid, Schwartz said, making it easier to deploy in times of crisis.
“Central banks can more easily lend their gold there to other banking institutions.”
John Plassard, an analyst at Cite Gestion Private Bank, said the Dutch move was intended “for there to be more immediate availability in the event of a crisis”.
For the moment, it was a “fairly one-off move”, but he warned that if other central banks followed suit, it could damage confidence in the US.
At the beginning of the year, there were concerns raised in Germany about the security of its central bank’s reserves in New York.
However, the powerful Bundesbank has decided for the moment not to shift its reserves away from New York.
“The New York Fed is and remains an important storage site for our gold,” the bank told public TV station ARD in January.

articles.title: Power, water problems impact billion-peso Oriental Mindoro tourism
articles.summary: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro – Persistent problems with power and water supply are affecting the tourism industry in Oriental Mindoro, according to the 2026 Local Tourism Product and Market Survey,…

blocks.text: CALAPAN CITY, Oriental Mindoro – Persistent problems with power and water supply are affecting the tourism industry in Oriental Mindoro, according to the 2026 Local Tourism Product and Market Survey, which was presented at the Oriental Mindoro Heritage Museum on September 2.

“Our problem in power and water impact our tourism industry. Just like in Puerto Galera and other tourist destinations, the frequent brownouts and water shortage discourage tourist from coming back,” said Dhon Calda, head of Oriental Mindoro’s Provincial Tourism Office (PTO) . In March, the local government of Puerto Galera declared a state of water emergency after its water sources were
declared non potable.

From January 1 to August 16 this year, a total of 684,622 tourists visited multiple destinations in the province, Calda said. The figure is lower than the 908,917 visitors in 2024 and the 1,035,705 guests in 2025.
The province’s total tourism sector revenue from 2024 to August 16 was P15,757,427,000, broken down to P6,251,413,000 in 2024, P6,392,732,500 last year, and P3,113,281,500 during the last 8 months.
Calda said the industry is expecting more tourist during the second peak season from October to December which could improve this year’s tourism performance.

Oriental Mindoro Electric Cooperative (Ormeco) Gen. Manager Engr. Humphrey Dolor conceded that power services has impacted tourism here. “It is correct that our power woes affect the industry but it is not the main contibutor. Look at Palawan, which has a worse power problem but their tourism industry is flourishing,” Dolor said in a message to the Inquirer.
But he pressed for support in resolving the cooperative’s struggles and asked people to refrain from finger-pointing. /jpv

articles.title: 'My students should be here': Tumbler Ridge teacher shares toll of deadly school shooting
articles.summary: One of the teachers caught in the deadly school shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary has shared her story publicly for the first time, alongside a series of new lawsuits against OpenAI that allege the…

image.caption: A memorial in Tumbler Ridge remembers the victims of the February mass shooting. (Tom Summer/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia·New

One of the teachers caught in the deadly school shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary has shared her story publicly for the first time, alongside a series of new lawsuits against OpenAI that allege the company should have warned Canadian officials about the shooter's ChatGPT activity.
Statement released along with series of new lawsuits against OpenAI from teachers, students and families

One of the teachers caught in the deadly school shooting at Tumbler Ridge Secondary has shared her story publicly for the first time, describing a "dark cloud" lingering over her hometown in the weeks and months following the tragedy.

Deidre Rushlow is one of the plaintiffs in a series of lawsuits filed this week in California against OpenAI, alleging the company's ChatGPT platform was used to help plan the shooting, which left eight victims, including five students and an educator at the school, dead.

Along with the lawsuit, Rushlow issued a written statement through the Canadian lawyers representing her in the case. In it, she says she is "haunted by the memory" of the day, calling it "a wound that sears with unending pain for my entire community."
Her letter is a rare insight into what people who were at Tumbler Ridge Secondary experienced, with the town's leaders asking for privacy as they recover from the tragedy.

"My name is Deidre Rushlow. Up until February 10, 2026, I was the English and Humanities teacher at Tumbler Ridge Secondary School. My students were in the library when the shooting happened. I did not know, nor could I know, that when I sent them to the library with my educational assistant, they were living their final moments," the statement begins.
Rushlow says she was in her first year of full-time teaching, having previously attended and graduated from the school before becoming a substitute.

"When I finally got the keys to my very own classroom last summer, I scrubbed each corner clean, added personal touches to brighten it up, and spent days organizing it until every last detail was perfect for my students," she writes.

"That same classroom has now been reduced to a pile of dust, all of my supplies and decorations packed into boxes and stored somewhere unknown to me. The career that once brought me such joy now terrifies me in ways I never imagined possible. How can I ever be responsible for another parent’s child again?"
RCMP identify all 8 victims of shooting in Tumbler Ridge, B.C.
"My students should be here getting ready for the next school year," she says. "Instead, their families, friends and classmates are left behind to suffocate in limitless grief and trauma."
Investigation ongoing as new school year begins
As the school year begins, students at Tumbler Ridge Secondary will be back in portable classrooms that were set up in the wake of the shooting.
The school itself, which housed students from grades 7 to 12, is being demolished and replaced by a new facility funded by the provincial and federal governments.
The municipality is also working with those higher levels of government to develop a recovery plan and to continue offering supports to those who need it.
The police investigation into the deadly day is also ongoing, RCMP say, with a coroner's inquest planned once that is complete.

items: Unsealed documents reveal details of RCMP's response, investigation into Tumbler Ridge shooting
Tumbler Ridge school demolition 'new chapter' in recovery after shooting, residents say

blocks.text: 'We will not forgive, we will not forget,' teacher says
Recent scrutiny has been centred on OpenAI after it was revealed that the shooter's ChatGPT account had been flagged internally, without warning Canadian officials or law enforcement.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has since apologized and says new policies are in place to offer better protections.
Teachers, students file 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting

But as part of the lawsuits filed this week though U.S. class-action firm Edelson PC, it is claimed OpenAI's leadership "ignored its own safety staff and refused to alert police," instead "choosing profit over the lives of the children of Tumbler Ridge" as it prepares to become a publicly-traded company."

Jason Kwon, chief strategy officer at OpenAI, said in a response posted on X that those claims are false and that his team works "hard to define standards and processes for when to report cases to law enforcement and to apply those standards to really difficult and complex situations."

items: Teachers, students file new wave of lawsuits against OpenAI over Tumbler Ridge shooting

blocks.text: The lawsuits and their claims will be tested in court in California, where OpenAI is headquartered.
In her statement, Rushlow writes she wants accountability for the company.
"We will not forgive, we will not forget, and we certainly will not rest until every last individual at OpenAI who was complicit in the Tumbler Ridge shooting has been brought to justice," she says.

articles.title: China’s falling emissions amid Iran war spark hope of decarbonisation watershed
articles.summary:
Oil consumption plummets and EV sales soar as analysts say demand may not fully return even if crude price falls

China’s carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% after the outbreak of the…

blocks.text: China’s carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% after the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran, thanks to a sharp reduction in oil consumption and a steady rise in the use of electric vehicles and public transport, analysis shows.

The report reveals the role of clean energy in cushioning the price shocks caused by the strait of Hormuz crisis to the world’s biggest oil importer. It also reinforces hopes that China, which is the world’s biggest greenhouse gas emitter, may be nearing a turning point in decarbonising its economy.

China was able to increase overall transportation use, despite cutting oil imports by 32%, according to second-quarter energy data reported by the country’s National Bureau of Statistics and analysed for Carbon Brief by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.

The reduction – equivalent to about a million barrels a day – from the world’s biggest petro-customer helped to stabilise global oil prices, which nevertheless surged by about 60% in the weeks and months after the first US airstrikes in late February.

How that was achieved has been the subject of considerable speculation. The analysis indicates that about two-thirds of the fall in imports came from running down, rather than building up, strategic oil stockpiles. The remaining third was largely covered by a reduction in demand.

blocks.caption: Wind turbines on the Yellow Sea coast of Yancheng, China. Photograph: Alex Plavevski/EPA

blocks.text: The country’s use of oil fell by 9% overall and by 16% for transport. While large numbers of petrol and diesel vehicles stayed off the roads, there was a surge in journeys by electric cars, buses, trains and trucks.

This electrifying trend had begun long before the strait of Hormuz crisis. China is by far the world’s biggest manufacturer, user and exporter of batteries, e-vehicles, wind turbines and solar panels. The disruption of oil supplies from the Gulf has strengthened the economic and strategic imperative of reducing petro-dependence.
In the first half of 2026, China’s shift towards electric vehicles displaced the equivalent of the UK’s entire oil consumption over a six-month period.
after newsletter promotion

Analysts predict much of this demand will not return even if global oil prices fall. “In a qualitative sense, there’s no question that the transport sector decarbonisation has been accelerated,” said Lauri Myllyvirta, the lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air. “It’s a validation of the energy security strategy that China has in place … It’s very clear that electrification is the winning strategy to insure against these kinds of shocks.”
Myllyvirta noted this was the first time China’s overall emissions had fallen due to a reduction in oil use rather than in coal consumption.

In fact, coal generation rose during the quarter due to shifting economic incentives and delays in adapting the country’s grid, which caused considerable wastage of wind and solar power. Despite this, observers believe the longer-term trend in China is away from fossil fuels.

Dr Muyi Yang, a senior analyst at Ember, which will next week publish a separate overview of China’s energy trends, said a fossil fuel peak was coming into view at the provincial and sectoral level. “The Iran crisis reinforces the case. The way China has been able to absorb its impact strengthens the confidence to go deeper and further.

“The risk of oil-import dependence increasingly comes from the geopolitical domain. This is a risk no country can effectively manage. So the more effective strategy is to reduce that exposure altogether. And China’s experience is demonstrating that this works.”

articles.title: Pilandok exits PAR early Thursday morning
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) exited the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) early Thursday morning and is not expected to directly affect the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Storm Pilandok (international name: Krovanh) exited the Philippine area of responsibility (PAR) early Thursday morning and is not expected to directly affect the country, according to the state weather bureau.

In the 5 a.m. weather forecast of the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), weather specialist Leanne Loreto said that Pilandok exited the PAR as of 4:30 a.m.

It was last estimated 1,030 kilometers east-northeast of Extreme Northern Luzon as of 4 a.m. It maintained its strength as it was still carrying a maximum wind speed of 75 kilometers per hour (kph) and gustiness of up to 90 kph.
“Less likely na papasok ito sa PAR ulit at hindi na rin makakaapekto sa panahon,” Loreto said.
(It is less likely to re-enter the PAR and this will not affect the weather conditions.)
Meanwhile, Loreto said that the southwest monsoon or habagat will continue to prevail in parts of Luzon on Thursday.

She noted that habagat will bring significant rainfall (50 to 100 millimeters) over Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, La Union, Pangasinan, Abra, Benguet, Zambales, Bataan, and Occidental Mindoro on Thursday.

She added that Metro Manila, Cagayan Valley, the rest of Cordillera Administrative Region, the rest of Central Luzon, Cavite, Batangas, Rizal, Laguna, and Oriental Mindoro will experience scattered rainshowers and thunderstorms due to habagat.
On the other hand, Visayas and Mindanao will see hot and humid weather conditions with low chances of rainshowers.
Gale warning was also raised in Batanes and Western Babuyan Islands. /jpv

articles.title: Groups file petition for probe, review of Subic Freeport development
articles.summary: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — A coalition of environmental and community groups petitioned Malacañang on Tuesday (Sept. 1) seeking an independent probe into the fatal landslide at the Tipo High-Tech Eco…

blocks.text: SAN ANTONIO, Zambales — A coalition of environmental and community groups petitioned Malacañang on Tuesday (Sept. 1) seeking an independent probe into the fatal landslide at the Tipo High-Tech Eco Park in the Subic Bay Freeport and a wider review of major development projects in the area.

The Save Subic Bay Coalition, composed of residents, Ayta communities, business groups and civil society organizations, made the appeal in a petition addressed to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., the Senate and the House of Representatives.

“In light of the flood-control controversy and the severe flooding affecting communities, particularly Olongapo, we respectfully call for an independent and comprehensive review of major developments in the freeport, especially those near waterways, slopes, forests and mangroves,” according to Jen Velarmino-van der Heijde, spokesperson of the coalition and president of Subic Bay Chamber for Health and Environment Conservation. She said the petition was received by the Office of the President on Tuesday.
“This is not about blaming or singling out any developer, but about transparency, accountability and public safety,” Velarmino-van der Heijde told the Inquirer.

In their 10-page petition, the coalition asked authorities to determine the actual causes of the landslide, including whether factors beyond prolonged rainfall contributed to the failure of a retaining structure or slope-protection system at the development along Tipo Road.
“While rainfall may have contributed to the failure, the public deserves an independent determination of the actual causes and contributing factors,” the coalition said in the petition.

Among the matters it wants investigated are whether the retaining structure was designed for the site’s geological, hydrological and seismic conditions; whether it was built according to approved engineering plans; whether surrounding slopes and earthworks were properly designed and stabilized; and whether drainage systems and construction activities contributed to slope instability.
The coalition also wants authorities to verify the project’s permits, environmental clearances and safety certifications and determine whether government inspections were properly conducted.

It said the investigation should cover the developer, contractors, consultants, engineers, permitting authorities and government agencies involved in approving, monitoring or supervising the development.

“No private entity or government agency should be presumed guilty before the facts are established. However, neither should any entity be shielded from accountability if an independent investigation establishes responsibility,” the coalition said.
Wider review
The coalition is also seeking a review of major developments within the Freeport, particularly those near environmentally sensitive areas, waterways, slopes, forests and mangroves.

It wants authorities to assess whether these projects comply with applicable laws, regulations and approved master plans, including their cumulative effects on drainage, flooding, slope stability, infrastructure and surrounding communities.

The petition also asks authorities to revisit the planning principles established for the Subic Bay Freeport, including the Development Master Plan prepared with the participation of Japanese urban planner Kenzo Tange and Kenzo Tange Associates.

It said current and proposed developments should be assessed against those principles and existing standards, including the relationship between building height and development density and the operational and safety requirements of the Subic Bay International Airport.

The coalition also wants the government to review major development contracts where significant environmental, geological, engineering or disaster risks have not been adequately established, including whether implementation should be suspended where legally warranted to ensure that economic activity does not compromise public safety or environmental protection.
Mangroves, railway project

The petition likewise calls for the protection of remaining mangroves within the Freeport and surrounding coastal areas, citing the proposed Subic-Clark Railway Project and its potential impact on more than six hectares of mangroves.

The coalition wants project proponents to examine technically feasible alternative alignments to avoid the affected mangrove areas and to make relevant environmental and technical studies available for public scrutiny.
“Where a project can be moved, move the project—not the mangrove,” the coalition said.
It also called for an updated inventory and mapping of remaining mangrove areas and independent environmental and technical reviews of major projects that could affect them.
Documents sought

The coalition is seeking public access, subject to lawful confidentiality requirements, to key documents related to the Tipo development, including engineering and structural plans, geotechnical and soil studies, drainage and hydrological studies, environmental compliance documents, permits, inspection reports and construction certifications.

It also wants relevant records on the developers and contractors involved, government inspections and enforcement actions, and the environmental and technical studies for the proposed railway alignment.

The Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) has said it supports an independent and comprehensive investigation into the Tipo incident and a review of its policies and practices to strengthen safeguards, monitoring and enforcement.

Xantheng (Subic) International Corp. (XSIC), the management arm of Tipo High-Tech Eco Park, earlier said it would cooperate with the investigation, assist affected families and monitor the area. The company attributed the incident to prolonged heavy rainfall in the Subic Bay Freeport and surrounding areas. /jpv

articles.title: Metro Manila eyes underground cisterns at 5 priority flood projects
articles.summary: Underground cisterns are planned beneath open spaces across Quezon City and Manila.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 7:00am
MMDA Chairman Don Artes explained during a press briefing in Malacañang on September 2, 2026, how the planned floodwater collection sites can help curb Metro Manila flooding.
Screenshot / RTVM
MANILA, Philippines — The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority has picked five projects to lead a planned network of 39 flood-catchment sites across Metro Manila.

At a press briefing at Malacañang, MMDA Chairman Don Artes said they aim to to finish the first batch by June 2027 as the capital looks for ways to keep intense rainfall from overwhelming its drainage systems.

The priority projects cover Miriam College, Camp Aguinaldo and the University of the Philippines Diliman in Quezon City, and Rizal Memorial Sports Complex and a combined Rajah Sulayman Park-Remedios Circle project in Manila.

Artes said the underground cisterns will be built beneath open spaces at the priority locations to temporarily hold rainwater instead of allowing it to immediately enter drainage systems and waterways.
The MMDA will present the projects to Executive Secretary Ralph Recto and Budget Secretary Kim Robert de Leon for possible funding.
Artes said the remaining projects among the 39 identified sites could be completed by December 2027 if funding is secured.
'Manage' the water
The projects form part of a broader "sponge city" and nature-based approach that uses different methods to absorb, retain or slow down rainwater.

“Sabi nga po nung isang ekspertong kausap namin with the advent po ng climate change, extreme weather conditions, heavy downpour…hindi na dapat i-control yung tubig, hindi na dapat labanan kung hindi dapat po ay i-manage,” Artes said.
(“As one of the experts we consulted said, with the advent of climate change, extreme weather conditions, heavy downpour… we should no longer control or fight the water, but instead manage it.”)
Among the approaches identified for the 39 sites are underground cisterns and bioretention areas, mangrove forests, permeable surfaces and green parks with permeable sidewalks.
Some waterways may also undergo river renaturation, which involves restoring more natural features and vegetation near bodies of water to help manage flooding.
Artes said each Metro Manila local government identified two to three possible locations where different flood-management approaches could be applied.
Funding still being worked out
Artes said the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank has indicated up to $200 million in financing for the projects, although the amount and financing terms have yet to be finalized.
AIIB, a multilateral financial instituion, also supported the feasibility study for the proposed projects, which was conducted with Netherlands-based engineering consultancy Haskoning.
"It's a lending institution. Partner po kasi siya ng World Bank doon sa initial na ibinigay pong pondo sa Metro Manila Flood Management Project na patapos na po," Artes said.
("It's a lending institution. It was also the World Bank's partner in providing funding for the Metro Manila Flood Management Project, which is nearing completion.")
The feasibility study initially considered 107 sites before the list was narrowed to 39 following consultations and assessments.

articles.title: Air Canada Express flight attendants vote on strike mandate as contract talks stall
articles.summary: Flight attendants who work on Air Canada Express flights are voting on whether to authorize strike action as their union says bargaining talks have stalled.

image.caption: An Air Canada Express aircraft takes off from Vancouver International Airport in July. The union for Air Canada Express flight attendants is seeking a strike mandate after months of collective bargaining. (Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Business·New
Flight attendants who work on Air Canada Express flights are voting on whether to authorize strike action as their union says bargaining talks have stalled.
Union says it hasn't been able to reach agreement with employer on 'critical issues'

The Canadian Flight Attendant Union, which represents around 1,000 flight attendants, says it's seeking a strike mandate after being unable to reach an agreement with Jazz Aviation on "the most critical issues" despite nine months of negotiations and enlisting the services of a mediator.

"The CFAU believes a strong strike mandate from its membership is necessary to ensure Jazz Aviation understands the seriousness of the outstanding issues and the resolve of its members," the news release said.
A spokesperson for Jazz Aviation said the company remains committed to reaching an agreement at the bargaining table "without disruption to its operations."
The company is seeking out the appointment of a conciliation officer as negotiations with the Canadian Flight Attendant Union have reached an impasse, the spokesperson said in an email.
Jazz Aviation serves as the primary operator for Air Canada Express flights. It is not owned by Air Canada but by a holding company called Chorus.
Union suggests safety, pay among key issues
The union's news release doesn't outline what those issues are specifically, but suggests safety and pay are among them.
The importance of safety was highlighted in March after the fatal accident involving Air Canada Express Flight AC8646 at LaGuardia Airport, which killed both pilots, the news release says.

items: LaGuardia air traffic control staffing might have violated procedures night of Air Canada collision
WestJet flight attendants vote to ratify new collective agreement

blocks.text: "Safety does not begin at takeoff, nor does it end at landing," said Marsha Walters, president of the Canadian Flight Attendant Union, in the release.
"It begins with fair working conditions, proper rest, and respect for the flight attendants who are responsible for the safety and care of passengers every day."
Walters goes on to say that any work required by its members "should be credited."
"If the time belongs to the employer, it should be compensated. And if flight attendants are safety professionals, they must be treated and compensated accordingly."
Former flight attendant on why she quit the industry
Voting closes on Friday at noon. The vote comes just weeks after WestJet flight attendants went on strike and a little over a year after more than 10,000 Air Canada flight attendants did the same.
It's unclear when Air Canada Express flight attendants could walk off the job if they vote in favour of a strike mandate.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Sarah Petz is a Toronto-based senior writer with the CBC News live pages team. Born and raised in Manitoba, her career has taken her across three provinces, multiple cities and to northern Uganda.

articles.title: Complaints raised of excessive force by RCMP in Sheshatshiu Innu Nation as video circulates
articles.summary: Dozens of people protested outside the RCMP detachment in Happy Valley-Goose Bay on Wednesday following the arrest of a man that was recorded and posted online by his girlfriend, who called the…

image.caption: A still image taken from a video taken by Nerissa Rich showing the arrest of her boyfriend by members of the RCMP. (Nerissa Rich/Facebook)

blocks.text: Nfld. & Labrador·New

Dozens of people protested outside the RCMP detachment in Happy Valley-Goose Bay on Wednesday following the arrest of a man that was recorded and posted online by his girlfriend, who called the actions by the police officers excessive.
Warning: This story contains descriptions of a video that shows violent interactions

Innu leadership and members of the Sheshatshiu Innu First Nation are accusing members of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police of using excessive force in an arrest — which was recorded and posted online — at a home in Sheshatshiu Tuesday night.
"If they don't want to be here, they can move on," Sheshatshiu Innu First Nation Chief Eugene Hart said of the officers, speaking to the CBC on Wednesday.
Hart joined several dozen people outside the local RCMP detachment in protest, while awaiting release of the man taken into custody.
The arrest was prompted by a call from the man's girlfriend, Nerissa Rich. She said he was drunk at the time and her hope was police would take him to one of their holding cells to sleep it off.
She said it was an unusual situation for the family, that there was no violence involved, but it seemed like the right call in the moment.

"I don't want him to bother people at the house and especially with my kids there. So I only want him to go here [to the detachment] and sleep it off and I pick him up in the morning. But that's not what happened," she said, waiting for his release.

Her boyfriend, who is not being named by CBC, has been charged with four counts of unlawfully assaulting a peace officer with a weapon or causing bodily harm, two charges of resisting or obstructing a peace officer and one count of mischief relating to property.

The video posted to social media by Rich begins with officers already inside the home. Three police officers have their hands on the man, as he stands against an exterior door. A dog is continuously barking throughout the incident.
There are shouts from people inside the home, including Rich, towards the officers, who try to restrain the man.
At one point, as the man turns his body and tries to pull an arm away, one of the officers takes his hand from the man's wrist, and hits him in the face.
Shouts and screams erupt, as the same officer threatens to arrest one of the onlookers. Not long after, the same officer proceeds to punch the man the police are trying to arrest.
That prompts Nerissa Rich to scream about her boyfriend being punched in the face.
"I'm fucking recording you!," she yells at the officers.
"My son is here!" she yells.
The man is taken to the ground. At one point, he wraps his arm around the leg of the officer who had punched him.
"He just spit in his face," says another officer of the man on the ground, turning to Rich, standing between her and the ongoing arrest.
The officer who previously threw a punch then punches the man on the ground again, three more times, before using his stun gun.
Rich screams: "Stop!" At one point, screaming, she calls the officers "assholes."
Not long after, a second officer told Rich to back up, or she would also be taken to jail, before the video ends. It captures just under two minutes in total.
'It felt like I had to do something'
Lorraine Rich, who is the aunt of the man who was arrested, said she got through only part of the video on social media, before deciding to take action.
"It felt like I had to do something," Lorraine Rich said, while also waiting outside the detachment.
She called for community members to join in protest outside of the detachment Wednesday.
"I said this morning somebody is going to get killed by the cops if something isn't done," she said.
Innu Nation is calling for change in the way policing is done in their communities
Innu Nation Grand Chief Jodie Ashini joined the gathering in Sheshatshiu, saying the video shows what is "clearly excessive force."
"I feel it's more of a systemic racism problem," she said, suggesting there have been other objectionable incidents spoken of by community members, not captured on video.
"They're continuing that long history of colonial power and abuse," she said.
Hart and Ashini said they have asked for removal of one officer in the video and asked that he not be sent to any other detachments on reserves.
"I made it clear in [the detachment]. He is no longer welcome," Hart said.

They also said they would like to see the establishment of a tribal police service for the First Nation, being an autonomous police service managed by the community. That has been an ask "for years" and would have to involve action by both the provincial and federal governments.
CBC News has contacted the RCMP, but has yet to receive a response to questions.

"When you have a severe thunderstorm cell, you do have the potential for there to be a twist," she said. "But you don't even need a tornado to have damaging winds and dangerous situations."

TLC and Salt N Pepa show cancelledAmy van den BergA TLC and Salt N Pepa show with En Vogue at RBC Ampitheatre has been cancelled tonight due to "severe weather," according to a post by the venue to the social media platform X.It has been rescheduled to Sept. 11, the post said.

Watch out for some TTC delaysAlina SnisarenkoIf you're planning to take the TTC on your commute home, be prepared for some delays. The transit agency has put out a number of alerts on social media.Trains aren't stopping at St. Patrick station on Line 1 due to flooding and there is no service between Finch West and Humber College stations on Line 6 due to debris on the tracks. For bus routes, the TTC has warned of a detour on its 18 Caledonia bus route due to flooding. There is also no service at St Clair West station's bay 3, which services the 512 streetcar route, due to flooding. You can find the latest on delays here.

GO Transit services disruptedAmy van den BergThere are "significant delays" on the Lakeshore West and Milton lines, according to the GO Transit website. The Lakeshore East and Barrie line is listed as having "minor delays."

More stormy weather in the pipelineAlina SnisarenkoThe thunderstorm that hit shortly after 5 p.m. isn't the end of it, according to Environment Canada's forecast for Toronto. The weather agency says showers will become mixed with thunderstorms until midnight, with the risk of a thunderstorm overnight. As for rainfall, local amounts of 30 to 40 millimeters can be expected, with a low of 20 millimeters.

Around 65,000 customers without power: Toronto HydroAlina SnisarenkoToronto Hydro says around 65,000 customers are affected by widespread outages from the storm. Brie Davis, spokesperson for the agency, said crews are "working to restore service safely and as quickly as possible." "Given the scale of the storm and the number of outages, restoration efforts may take time and vary by location. Additional storms are forecast throughout the evening, which may impact restoration efforts," said Davis.

A community cleanupAlina SnisarenkoFlooding on a residential street near Mt. Pleasant Road and Eglinton Avenue E. The city is dealing with flooding after a destructive thunderstorm hit juts after 5 p.m. Wednesday. (Alina Snisarenko/CBC News)I live near Mt. Pleasant Road and Eglinton Avenue E., and just got a nice message from my roommate about cleanup efforts underway on our street. A number of our neighbours went outside to help deal with flooding on our street, working to clear debris from the rainwater catch basins to try and get the water flowing. The team effort seems to be working, as I just got an update over text that the water has started to come down.

Roof torn off Brampton buildingJohn RietiA building on Automatic Drive was severely damaged by Wednesday afternoon's storm. As of 6:14 p.m., Brampton is under an orange watch for a severe thunderstorm. (Jacob Estrin/CBC)Freelance videographer Jacob Estrin sent this image from Brampton where a building on Automatic Road had its roof torn off by the storm's winds. Estrin reported that debris from the building is scattered across nearby Williams Parkway.

What we saw from the newsroomAlina SnisarenkoAt around 5 p.m. I was just about to finish up a story in the newsroom and head out, when I decided to take a peek out of the office windows to get a glimpse of what my commute home would look like. It did not look inviting in the least bit. I saw a constant wall of rain sweeping through the street, and the heavy winds sent a branch falling down and caused street lights to violently swing from the downpour. An abnormality: city pylons. They were lined up along the road and did not move … at all. Kind of a remarkable sight when you see everything else swaying from such a massive storm.I'm still in the office right now, and while I noticed a slight brightening after the initial onslaught, the skies are back to being very dim right now. Quite eerie!

Alerts ring out in PATHJohn RietiLike many Torontonians in the downtown core, we were walking out for dinner when the storm hit. Environment Canada’s alerts rang out from dozens of phones around us in Toronto’s underground PATH system about “destructive winds and very large hail.” Luckily, everyone was already underground.Within minutes of the rain beginning, however, water was pouring through the ceiling in one of the underground hallways.

articles.title: Candidate for Quebec Conservatives apologizes for 2020 post about euthanizing pro-vaccine people
articles.summary: A candidate for the Conservative Party of Quebec is apologizing for online comments he made at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. He wrote that Quebecers in favour of vaccines should be euthanized.…

image.caption: David Alarie, a candidate for the Conservative Party of Quebec apologized for comments he made in 2020 in which he said "those who believe that the government is doing the right things, the only vaccine owed to you is euthanasia." (Facebook / Candidat Parti conservateur du Québec Brome-Missisquoi)

blocks.text: Montreal·New

A candidate for the Conservative Party of Quebec is apologizing for online comments he made at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic. He wrote that Quebecers in favour of vaccines should be euthanized. Just seven days into the election campaign, several other candidates in various parties have faced pushback and even calls to resign.
Other candidates from other parties also faced backlash, calls to step down

A candidate for the Conservative Party of Quebec (PCQ) is apologizing for comments he made at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic during which he wrote that Quebecers in favour of vaccines should be euthanized.
David Alarie, now a PCQ candidate in Brome-Missisquoi, in the Eastern Townships, said he had shared those thoughts “in the heat of the moment.”

In a Facebook post from Nov. 19, 2020, Alarie wrote: “I’ve been holding back for too long. Those who believe that the government is doing the right things, the only vaccine owed to you is euthanasia.”
Months later, on Jan. 19, 2021, he said the only way to get the CAQ government out of power was to harass their MNAs and demand their resignation.
In an emailed statement sent to Radio-Canada following questions sent to the party, Alarie now says these comments were “clumsy” and do not reflect his current thinking or that of the PCQ.
“In the middle of the pandemic, I wanted to show a bit of humour, but I recognize today that it was in bad taste,” read his statement.

During the 2022 election campaign, a CBC News investigation found that of the first 54 candidates the party had announced, nearly 30 per cent have used their social media accounts during the pandemic to amplify medical misinformation, conspiracy theorists or to engage with far-right extremists.
This election campaign, several other party candidates have had past comments highlighted in traditional media outlets.
Asked about some of those cases on Wednesday, PCQ Leader Éric Duhaime said the Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) is “digging dirt.”
“It's the kind of tactics that are understandable from a very unpopular government who has a terrible track record,” he said.
“I'm telling Mrs. [Christine] Fréchette, she needs to elevate the debate a little bit. Stop asking her employees to dig dirt and start to talk about her own track record.”
Just seven days into the election campaign, several other candidates in various parties have faced pushback and even calls to resign.
CAQ candidate and comments made to a women’s centre
This past week, the CAQ candidate in the Ungava riding pulled out of the race after comments he made at the Centres de femmes Les Elles Nord — a women’s centre located in Chibougamau, Que.

In a news release, the organization states that the candidate, Paul Dadie, visited its premises without an appointment to discuss the centre's activities and mission, and the director made herself available to meet with him.

During the exchange, Dadie questioned the centre's women-only policy, the access reserved exclusively for women in certain spaces, as well as the fact that the organization does not hire men, according to a news release issued by the organization on Tuesday.
“He also expressed the idea that men also had a say and an opinion to offer regarding the realities experienced by women," the statement reads.

"The tone and posture adopted by the candidate during this meeting created a confrontational climate rather than a genuine dialogue. The director was interrupted several times and could barely finish her responses.”
CAQ Party Leader Christine Fréchette confirmed on social media that the candidate was withdrawing and had offered his apologies. She described his behaviour as unacceptable.
Controversy surrounding PQ candidate
Parti Québécois (PQ) candidate in the Charlevoix–Côte-de-Beaupré riding, François Gariépy, was embroiled in controversy even before the election campaign began.

In recent weeks, there's been a consistent spotlight on the former journalist's past statements, including a podcast episode during which he used a slur against Indigenous women and another instance where he was accused of mocking women 55 and older.
So far, St-Pierre Plamondon has acknowledged the comments were inapproriate but said he had no intention of asking the candidate to withdraw.

In a post on X Wednesday afternoon he referred to statements made by Duhaime, saying he was in line with him on this and said he doesn’t care “about the misadventures of the PCQ candidates in 2014, or those of other parties.”
“We’ve seen enough of the anecdotal distractions concocted by the CAQ to keep up from talking about their track record and campaigning on our proposals and ideas,” he wrote.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Rachel Watts is a journalist with CBC News in Quebec City. Originally from Montreal, she enjoys covering stories in the province of Quebec. You can reach her at rachel.watts@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Epstein survivors urge billionaire Leon Black to cooperate with House panel
articles.summary:
Black called on to comply with subpoenas and appear as required to clarify connections to convicted sex offender

More than a dozen survivors of

blocks.text: More than a dozen survivors of Jeffrey Epstein’s abuse have called on the billionaire Leon Black to appear before the House oversight committee in order to clarify his connections to the late disgraced financier and convicted sex offender.
In a letter released on Wednesday, the survivors urged Black to comply with congressional subpoenas ahead of Thursday’s deposition before the House oversight committee.

“We are survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s abuse and exploitation, and we are calling on Leon Black to appear as required before the House oversight committee on Thursday,” the statement said. “We are also calling on Black to fully comply with the committee’s subpoenas, including its demand that he produce all responsive nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in his possession.”

Black, the New York private equity investor, paid Epstein tens of millions of dollars in fees during work he has described as tax and estate-planning services. He has already faced accusations of purposely delaying and disrupting the panel’s inquiry.

The letter further stated that “Black’s use of NDAs underscores why Congress must scrutinize the agreements in his possession and determine whether they shed light on his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and others in Epstein’s orbit”.
“If Black continues to withhold responsive records or refuses to comply with the committee’s demands, Congress should use every tool available to enforce its subpoenas.”
Last week, the Republican chairman of the House oversight committee, James Comer, threatened to hold Black in contempt if he fails to fully cooperate with the panel’s investigation into Epstein.
Black had not yet confirmed his appearance before the committee as of Tuesday, a person familiar with the matter had told the Guardian.

In a previous statement before the oversight committee in June, Black denied knowledge of Epstein’s crimes, writing: “I did not know about this nefarious activity until Epstein was charged with trafficking in July 2019.”
However, Black acknowledged that he was aware that Epstein had pleaded guilty in 2008 “to state charges relating to prostitution involving a minor”.

In a speech from the House floor this week, Thomas Massie, the Kentucky Republican who recently lost his primary to a challenger backed by Donald Trump, read aloud the names of several friends and associates of Epstein, including Black.
Massie called on the Department of Justice to investigate the group of men and women whom the representative referred to as “perpetrators” of Epstein’s crimes.
Massie also emphasized that despite the fact it has been nearly a year since Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, millions of the Epstein files remain unreleased.

articles.title: Poa admits he also faces liability if VP found guilty
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Michael Poa, who served as Vice President Sara Duterte’s chief of staff, undersecretary for finance and spokesperson at the Department of Education (DepEd), acknowledged on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Michael Poa, who served as Vice President Sara Duterte’s chief of staff, undersecretary for finance and spokesperson at the Department of Education (DepEd), acknowledged on Wednesday that he could face liability if Duterte is found guilty of misusing millions of pesos in confidential funds, while maintaining that he had no personal knowledge of how the money was used.

Poa, now one of Duterte’s defense lawyers but testifying as a hostile prosecution witness on Day 21 of her impeachment trial, also said he learned about the unusual names appearing in acknowledgment receipts for confidential fund payments only during congressional hearings in 2024, even though he had prepared DepEd’s response to a Commission on Audit (COA) audit observation memorandum (AOM) questioning P112.5 million in confidential expenditures.

Asked by Senator-judge Risa Hontiveros whether Office of the Vice President (OVP) and DepEd personnel could be held accountable if Duterte were found liable, Poa said: “It’s possible. Just being objective, Your Honor.”
Hontiveros then asked if Poa himself could face liability.
“It’s possible. I hope not, but possible,” he replied.
No operational role

Poa maintained that he had no operational role in handling the confidential funds. He said his involvement began only after he received the COA’s AOM flagging DepEd’s confidential fund reward payments. Before that, he said, he had no personal knowledge of how the funds were used.

After receiving the AOM, Poa said he approached then Undersecretary for Administration Nolasco Mempin to obtain proof of the success of activities supposedly funded through the rewards, particularly accomplishment reports.

Mempin, whom Poa said also had no personal knowledge of the funds’ use, eventually obtained certifications from Armed Forces of the Philippines officers, including Col. Manaros Boransing II and Col. Magtanggol Panopio.

But Boransing and Panopio told the impeachment court on Tuesday that they did not know their certifications would be used to support the liquidation of DepEd’s confidential expenditures. The two Army officers said their documents merely recorded participants’ attendance in eight Army-sponsored Youth Leadership Summits and 53 Information Education Campaign activities. They also testified that neither DepEd nor the OVP provided the AFP with confidential funds for those programs.
“Unfortunately, all that really came to me was this certification. So, that’s all I attached to our response to COA,” he said.
‘Impression’ and ‘theory’

Poa also softened his earlier explanation to the House that activities supported by the confidential funds were targeted based on information supplied by informants, describing that explanation as merely his “impression” and “theory.”

Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian pointed out that Poa’s written response to the COA sounded more definitive, making it appear that information from informants had directly contributed to successful operations.

“How do you now prove that this success is from confidential information, from payment of rewards? How do you connect this to a successful payment of reward that led to a successful operation?” Gatchalian asked.
He also told private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. that buying information from informants did not necessarily guarantee an immediately successful operation.

“Not all information purchased will necessarily result [in] immediate success,” Poa said when asked whether proof of success was required under Joint Circular 2015-01, which governs the use of confidential and intelligence funds.
Senator-judge Joel Villanueva questioned Poa on the basis for using AFP certifications to support DepEd’s P15.54 million in confidential fund expenditures.
‘Abogadong walang alam’

Poa said he did not consider the certifications in isolation, pointing to language in the documents referring to a “synergistic exchange of intelligence and information” that enabled authorities to identify areas where activities would be conducted.

The prosecution’s offer of Poa’s testimony triggered a sharp exchange after Tolosa described him as “ang abogadong walang alam (lawyer who knew nothing),” referring to his being tasked by Duterte to answer the COA despite repeatedly saying he did not know how the confidential funds were used.

Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison vehemently objected, saying Poa had rights under the trial rules to be protected from irrelevant, improper and insulting questions and from harsh or insulting treatment. Tolosa apologized and said he meant only that Poa had repeatedly testified in the House that he knew nothing about the funds.
Presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero ordered the phrase stricken from the record, saying it was discourteous and should not be used in referring to a fellow lawyer.
Names surfaced in House
Poa’s testimony also underscored the limits of his knowledge of the documents used to liquidate the confidential funds.

Asked by Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo whether he was familiar with names appearing in acknowledgment receipts submitted to the COA as proof of payment to supposed confidential informants, Poa said he did not remember seeing anything fictitious while at DepEd. He said he saw the unusual names only when the receipts were shown during the House inquiry in 2024, including the controversial “Mary Grace Piattos.”

When he asked former DepEd special disbursing officer Edward Fajarda for documents evidencing payments required for the COA audit, Poa said Fajarda initially handed him a sealed envelope, saying the documents were confidential.
