articles.title: Iranian attack on Saudi tanker killed two Filipino sailors, Saudi Arabia says
articles.summary: The kingdom condemns the targeting of Sidr, which was reportedly hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.

blocks.text: Saudi Arabia has condemned what it said was an Iranian attack on a Saudi-owned supertanker on Monday night that killed two Filipino sailors.
The Saudi national shipping company, Bahri, confirmed on Wednesday that its vessel Sidr was "involved in a security incident while transiting the Strait of Hormuz".

Sidr was hit by projectiles north of Oman's Musandam Peninsula, according to maritime security firms. A South Korean-owned supertanker, Senegal Prosperity, was reportedly struck east of Musandam around the same time.
Iran has not responded to the Saudi allegation. But it said earlier that two tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while using an unauthorised route through the strait.

The news of the sailors' deaths came after the US military carried out a wave of air strikes on Iran and Iranian forces targeted US bases in neighbouring Arab states with missiles and drones in their biggest exchange of fire since July.

On Wednesday Iran's health minister said 18 people were killed and 108 injured in the US attacks. Iran has accused the US of a "war crime" over a strike that killed four people including two children at a wedding party in the southern city of Sirik. The US military said it was looking into the reports.
Shipping company Bahri's statement said the unspecified "security incident" affecting Sidr happened in the Strait of Hormuz at around 23:40 local time (19:40 GMT) on Monday.

"It is with profound sadness that Bahri confirms the loss of two of its Filipino seafarers as a result of the incident," it added. "The company extends its deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathies to their families, loved ones, and colleagues during this difficult time."
Later, the Saudi foreign ministry expressed the kingdom's condemnation of "Iran's targeting of the Saudi tanker (Sidr) while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz".

It also condemned the recent Iranian attacks on Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait, and stressed the "need to halt escalation and respect the security and safety of international navigation", as well as the security of global energy supplies, national sovereignty, and international law.

The statements were issued a day after maritime risk management and intelligence firms Marisks and Kpler reported that two tankers each loaded with two million barrels of Saudi crude oil were struck by unknown projectiles within minutes of each other as they transited outbound through the Strait of Hormuz late on Monday.

Sidr was struck by "unknown projectiles" at 19:52 GMT about 16 nautical miles (30km) north-east of Khasab, Oman, while Senegal Prosperity was struck by "three unknown projectiles" about 17 nautical miles east of Khasab, according to Marisks.
The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency also reported two incidents in the same locations.

On Wednesday, Iran's Islamic Revolution Guard Corps said in a statement that two oil tankers sought "at the urging of the US military to transit via an illegal route" in the Strait of Hormuz before "striking mines and exploding". The vessels were "currently on fire", it added.

The US military has not commented, but it said the latest strikes on Iran followed "recent attempted attacks by the IRGC against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and against American service members".

The Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, has effectively been closed since the start of the US and Israel's war with Iran in February due to Iranian missile and drone attacks on commercial vessels and a US blockade of Iranian ports.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after the Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran has insisted it will not give up some measure of control over the waterway and has targeted vessels using a southern route through Omani waters that avoids its preferred route through Iranian waters.
Despite the Iranian attacks, US President Donald Trump has declared that the strait is "open" and the US military has been helping ships navigate the southern route.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said 17 million barrels of oil flowed through the Strait of Hormuz by ship on Monday - a record daily total since the start of the war.

articles.title: Napolcom probes police official’s assault on college student
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The National Police Commission (Napolcom) on Wednesday ordered an investigation into allegations that a police official assaulted and threatened to kill a college student. The…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Police Commission (Napolcom) on Wednesday ordered an investigation into allegations that a police official assaulted and threatened to kill a college student.

The complaint was filed by a 20-year-old student, who uses the alias “Ace,” against Senior Master Sgt. Don Carlos Almonidovar of the General Trias Component City Police Station over a road dispute on Aug. 27 at around 11:30 p.m.
Ace, who was driving a motorcycle in Trece Martires City, alleged that Almonidovar rammed his vehicle into his motorcycle, struck him with a firearm and threatened to kill him.
The incident occurred after Ace made a U-turn ahead of the police official’s vehicle, he alleged.
The 20-year-old and his companion were brought to the police station to settle the dispute, where Almonidovar was found to have consumed alcohol based on a breathalyzer test.

According to the commission, Almonidovar may face “administrative charges for grave misconduct and conduct unbecoming of a police officer.” He may also be dismissed from the service if the allegations are proven, it added.
Almonidovar, together with police investigators, was also directed to appear before Napolcom on Thursday to explain and respond to the complaint.

“We will not tolerate any police officer harming, oppressing, injuring, or intimidating ordinary citizens, or covering up such acts. As long as Napolcom exists, the public can count on us to take action and uphold their rights. This is for the people. You have my assurance,” Napolcom Commissioner Rafael Vicente Calinisan said in a statement. /das

articles.title: Romualdez lawyer questions Ombudsman’s fixation on client
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The lawyer of Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has lashed out against the Office of the Ombudsman anew, questioning why the constitutional body appears to be fixated on his…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The lawyer of Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin Romualdez has lashed out against the Office of the Ombudsman anew, questioning why the constitutional body appears to be fixated on his client when there is supposedly no evidence against him.

In a statement on Wednesday, Romualdez’s lawyer and spokesperson Ade Fajardo said he cannot understand why the Office of the Ombudsman is still bent on building a case against him when several individuals have already recanted their testimonies already or denied the claims of other witnesses.
“We cannot understand why they have been giving that much attention, why they have been singling out Rep. Romualdez when there’s no credible evidence against him,” he said.

Romualdez has been accused of facilitating budget insertions to implement anomalous infrastructure programs and receiving kickbacks from these projects. However, the lawmaker and his legal team have insisted that he is not involved in any wrongdoing, saying several times that as speaker, he does not have control over every step of the budget-making process in Congress.

“All of the high-ranking officials of the government were gone when the Maleta boys recanted their statements and others stated that they have no knowledge of the said deliveries, they were removed from the list and absolved. But the Ombudsman maintained the case against our client, making it seem that he is being singled out,” he said.
“That’s why we are confused why they are treating the former speaker this way. They seem to be making this too personal,” he added.

Fajardo did not mention who was the official who are the other officials that have been away from the spotlight or were absolved, but on Tuesday, several sources said that the Sandiganbayan had dropped plunder and graft charges against former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan — a co-accused in infrastructure scandal-related cases.
Other individuals supposedly behind the testimonies of 18 former bodyguards of ex-Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Elizaldy Co, along with Orly Guteza, have been arrested on other charges.

However, Sen. Rodante Marcoleta, the person alluded to by Guteza as behind his statements pinning down Romualdez, said it was “improbable” for him and former lawmaker Mike Defensor to conspire with the former Co bodyguard.

Fajardo has called out the Office of the Ombudsman several times in the past few days — saying last Aug. 27 that there is no reason to charge Romualdez if the Office of the Ombudsman no longer has any credible witness at hand.

Fajardo was referring to the recantations of Guteza, some of the 18 former Co bodyguards, and the testimony of 25 other drivers and security aides of Co and his family who have made testimonies that favor Romualdez’ case.
Fajardo said back then that even Bonoan supposedly did not link Romualdez to the flood control scam and alleged delivery of money in suitcases.
Then on Tuesday, Fajardo claimed that the Office of the Ombudsman is merely trying to keep its case against Romualdez alive by issuing statements.

Fajardo said that they disagree with Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano’s statements that the witnesses’ recantation can be considered additional evidence as they can be put next to each other to determine which is true.
What must be done, Fajardo stressed, is that comparisons between initial statements and recantations, as well as additional testimonies, should cure issues.
Earlier, Palace press officer Claire Castro said that while Romualdez’s camp is free to voice out opinions, the administration has just been following rules regarding due process and evidence.

Malacañang’s statements echo the speech of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in his fifth State of the Nation Address last July 27, as he said that while it is painful to see cases submitted against Romualdez, his cousin, it is the right thing to do. /das

articles.title: Netherlands moves billions in gold to London in 'crisis preparedness' move
articles.summary: The Dutch central bank removes some of its gold reserves from the US and Canada, saying it is because of "increasing geopolitical unrest".

blocks.text: The Dutch central bank (DNB) has confirmed that billions of dollars in gold has been taken out of north America and relocated to London, citing "increasing geopolitical unrest".

DNB said on Wednesday that 86 tonnes of gold had been removed from the US and Canada in a complex operation that took several months. It is now being held by the Bank of England, where the precious metal can be traded more easily "in a crisis situation".
Bank president Olaf Sleijpen said the move was "necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness".
The decision comes amid an ongoing trade dispute between the US and Canada, with both countries announcing fresh tariffs on each other after failed trade talks.
DNB said the transfer, which took place between March and August, saw 27 tonnes of gold bars moved from New York and Ottawa to Zeist in the Netherlands.
A similar quantity and quality was then moved to London, with no need to melt the bars down.
Exactly how so much gold was transported across the Atlantic Ocean has not been revealed.
The rest of the transfer was carried out by selling the gold in New York, and repurchasing it in London, the bank said, external.
"Combining the processes of buying and selling and physical transport has allowed DNB to spread the risks associated with such a complex physical gold relocation," the statement said.

DNB did not confirm what it was referring to with its mention of "geopolitical unrest" but the US economy remains in an uncertain position due to the country's ongoing war with Iran, which has impacted global trade.

Canada, meanwhile, has been hit hard by US tariffs on its key sectors of steel, aluminium, lumber and automobiles as well as an additional 50% levy on about C$28bn ($20bn; £15bn) of Canadian goods announced in August.

DNB said that gold that is held with the Bank of England "is regarded as the world's most easily tradable gold," and therefore more readily available in a crisis than if it was still in the US or Canada.
Prior to Wednesday's announcement, the DNB held 31.3% of its gold in New York and 19.7% in Ottawa. This has now fallen to 18.5% in both countries.
The total Dutch gold stock was 612.4 tonnes at the end of 2025 and has been valued at €72.2 billion, DNB said.
The bank's share of gold in London has increased from 18.1% to 32.1% after the move, while it still holds 30.8% of its reserves in the Netherlands.

articles.title: Burnham beware, the bond markets will demand proper answers in the budget | Nils Pratley
articles.summary:
Fair to say the current sell-off is international, but the PM has said little yet to make investors rethink the UK’s status

It’s too soon to say the bond markets have turned on Andy Burnham.…

blocks.text: It’s too soon to say the bond markets have turned on Andy Burnham. Tuesday’s spike in gilt yields, taking the UK’s 30-year borrowing costs to their highest level since 1998, was part of an international sell-off of government debt.

The main contributors are well-known. The Iran war, by increasing the cost of energy, has overturned the comforting start-of-the-year thesis of falling global inflation and interest rates. A plunging Japanese yen has kicked away another assumed source of financial stability. The US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, hasn’t calmed nerves with his solo, and so far futile, attempt to bring down US yields. Meanwhile, the early stage of the AI revolution is an exercise in issuing squillions of debt before long-term returns on capital can possibly be assessed meaningfully.

From the point of view of the mythical bond vigilante, in these circumstances it’s only logical to demand a higher return to lend to profligate governments with high debt ratios, which is most of them.

In a narrow sense, then, UK gilts were just moving with the market at a moment of rising financial risks in all directions. It’s just that the UK was already uncomfortably placed at the cold edge of the pack with the highest borrowing rates in the G7, a status largely reflecting a dismal 20-year record in keeping a lid on inflation and, especially now, a dependency on energy imports that stood at 43% in 2025.

It is also true, unfortunately, that six weeks into the job Burnham and the chancellor, John Healey, have said nothing to make bond investors rethink the UK’s status. Investors have heard the dutiful commitment to Rachel Reeves’s fiscal rules, but Burnham’s Commons speech on Tuesday carried little sense of urgency about the UK’s financial predicament, or appreciation of how 10-year gilt yields at 5.2% will cause damage if sustained for long.

More “public control” of utilities – the theme Burnham constantly returns to – may be desirable and play well on the backbenches. But, even when the ambiguous meaning is made clearer, how does it translate into, say, substantially lower costs of building infrastructure? Should it really be a top economic priority?

“Markets are sceptical that ‘devolution’ and ‘control’ are levers for lower government-led inflation,” said the Panmure Liberum economist Simon French. “Burnham/Healey’s unenviable task is to prove they are the right levers. If they fail then a very painful period of financial repression/demand side-led disinflation will be necessary.”

There is an uncomfortable sense that the bond market expects next month’s budget to be a bigger event than Burnham and Healey will produce. The tone of Burnham’s Commons speech was “the last thing investors wanted to hear”, said the former Goldman Sachs economist Jim O’Neill – quite a verdict from a friendly critic who was being lined up for a role in government until recently.

But one can see his point. He told the BBC that high government borrowing costs would force Labour to get real about dealing with the triple lock on the state pension and “excessive” welfare spending. There has been little rolling of the pitch, as they say in Westminster, in either of those directions to date.
after newsletter promotion

It may be, of course, that impressions are mistaken and that next month’s promised 10-year economic plan turns out to be a big exercise in addressing energy costs, defence spending, social care, housing shortages and all the other main challenges. But it is also easy to imagine an alternative script in which hard decisions are deferred and the UK-specific action in the bond market turns uglier – especially if, say, disruption to global energy markets looks likely to last the winter.

Labour has spent 2026 defenestrating one leader and anointing another. It needs something to show for it. Burnham speaks of giving businesses and consumers breathing space from the cost of living pressures. That task is easier when the government itself is getting some breathing space from the bond markets. Whatever the chosen mix of spending cuts and tax rises, the budget needs details.

articles.title: Sadiq Khan fined over untaxed car falsely registered in his name
articles.summary: London mayor’s office says he is ‘victim of a scam’ after conviction under fast-track system where magistrates can decide outcomes in seconds

blocks.text: Sadiq Khan’s office has revealed he was the victim of a scam that led to him being fined for failing to tax a car that did not belong to him.
The London mayor was found guilty last month under a system of “conveyor-belt justice”, in which magistrates decide on hundreds of cases a day, sometimes spending less than a minute on each.
City Hall officials say the 24-year-old Nissan Micra did not belong to Khan or Transport for London.

The mayor has been the focus of protests by motorists angry at the expansion of the ultra-low emission zone in London. Some said they planned to register cars in Khan’s name to make him liable for the £12.50 daily charge.

The prosecution was undertaken by the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency, which accused Khan of being the keeper of the vehicle when it was spotted as being untaxed on 24 January. In a move that paves the way for the conviction to be erased after a court hearing on Thursday, the DVLA said on Wednesday evening that the case had been withdrawn after a review and it was investigating the circumstances.
“This is a scam, which is a crime,” said a spokesperson for Khan.
“It’s not the first time the mayor has been the victim of a scam involving people falsely stating that Sadiq is the owner of a vehicle. Such behaviour is illegal, and the DVLA are aware.”

A magistrate, sitting in a private hearing of the single justice procedure in Herefordshire, convicted Khan in his absence and ordered that he pay a £220 fine, £85 in costs and settle the £35.84 bill for unpaid tax on the Micra.
PA Media alerted the DVLA to the criminal conviction on Tuesday and its officials confirmed they were reviewing the case and investigating the circumstances of the prosecution.
Court documents show that DVLA letters addressed to the mayor about the unpaid tax bill were sent to a Gordon Ramsay restaurant in east London instead of the nearby TfL offices.
The mayor faces the possibility of having to appear in court to try to overturn the conviction.
after newsletter promotion
The single justice procedure was introduced in 2015 as a cheaper method of dealing with low-level criminal cases, allowing magistrates to sit alone and in private.

The system, which is under government review, was criticised in 2024 when about 59,000 train-fare evasion convictions were overturned for being unlawful. It also emerged that children had been wrongly convicted in the secretive courts.
More scrutiny has come over repeated incidents of sick and incapacitated pensioners being convicted for not paying their household bills.
In Khan’s case, court records show he was prosecuted by the DVLA after the annual tax on the Micra, which was first registered in 2002, ran out last September.

articles.title: Alanis Morissette sues former tour manager over alleged 'calculated blackmail campaign'
articles.summary: In a lawsuit filed this week in California, Alanis Morissette is suing her former tour manager for what she calls a "calculated blackmail campaign," alleging Keren Urinov threatened to frame her for…

image.caption: Alanis Morissette attends the FIREAID Benefit Concert for California Fire Relief at Intuit Dome on Jan. 30, 2025, in Inglewood, Calif. (Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for FIREAID)

blocks.text: Entertainment

In a lawsuit filed this week in California, Alanis Morissette is suing her former tour manager for what she calls a "calculated blackmail campaign," alleging Keren Urinov threatened to frame her for drug trafficking unless the Canadian singer-songwriter agreed to sign her to a lengthy contract.
Lawsuit claims Keren Urinov threatened to frame Canadian singer-songwriter for drug trafficking

Alanis Morissette is suing her former tour manager for what she calls a "calculated blackmail campaign" to frame her for drug trafficking unless the Canadian singer-songwriter agreed to sign her to a lengthy contract.

Morissette filed a lawsuit in California on Tuesday, obtained by CBC News, alleging that Keren Urinov is threatening to report her to British authorities for drug trafficking unless Morissette agreed to employ her as a tour director for 15 years and pay her "massive compensation."

Morissette is suing Urinov for civil extortion, fraud and negligent misrepresentation, writing in the lawsuit that she "will not be coerced into delivering her blackmailer an extraordinary payday" and that she pursued legal action "to expose Urinov's scheme and hold her accountable."
What happened?
Urinov, who previously worked for Live Nation's Israeli operations, was hired in 2025 as a temporary tour manager for Morissette's world tour.
In July 2025, the singer and her team, including Urinov, were allegedly flying from the U.K. to Spain for a concert.

At the airport, the lawsuit claims a British Border Force official flagged a bag, asking who owned it. When Urinov said it was hers, she was arrested and issued a seizure notice alleging that the bag contained marijuana and xylazine — a non-opioid animal tranquilizer.

During questioning, Urinov allegedly admitted that the bag and the drugs were hers, showing the authorities her Israeli medical marijuana licence, the lawsuit says. It was returned to her and she was released.
The next day, Urinov was allegedly detained again at an airport for questioning about the bag they'd taken the previous day.
'A series of increasingly extortionate letters'
The suit claims Urinov told Morissette that — again — she admitted the bag and the drugs belonged to her.

But after the tour wrapped, Urinov and her lawyers allegedly sent "a series of increasingly extortionate letters to Morissette," threatening to sue her in the U.K. for "unspecified claims" if Morissette refused to tell British law enforcement that the drugs were hers.

According to the lawsuit, the letters said Morissette could "put an end to the matter" by giving Urinov a fixed 15-year contract that included "income equivalent to that of a tour director with annual increases and bonuses."

She also allegedly demanded Morissette arrange for an immigration lawyer to get a work visa that would allow Urinov to work in the United States — and that if the visa couldn't be obtained, she'd demand more pay.
'Reluctant' but 'no choice but to sue'
The lawsuit also details reasons Morissette felt Urinov "was a terrible manager of the 2025 tour."
This includes "unnecessarily" spending nearly $70,000 US after an "inexplicable error with a hotel booking that no competent tour manager would have made," the court filing states.

Morissette also alleges that while on tour, Urinov told the singer's team that she and a friend were arrested in Latin America "years ago" for smuggling drugs in a surfboard and that Urinov illegally fled the country after being released on bail.

"This was an astounding revelation, given that Urinov had told Morissette's team during her interview for the tour manager position that nothing in her past would cause any complications with obtaining visas or travelling, and she never mentioned her arrest or crimes in Latin America," the lawsuit states.

items: Watch Alanis Morissette and Sarah McLachlan perform with Olivia Rodrigo at Daisy Chain Fields

blocks.text: The lawsuit also says Morissette was "reluctant" to file, but that she had "no choice but to sue."
"Morissette will not agree to work with an incompetent blackmailer for the next 15 years or pay her a ransom under the gun," it reads.
Morissette is seeking a trial by jury. CBC News has reached out to Urinov and representatives for Morissette but has not yet heard back.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Griffin Jaeger is a reporter and producer with CBC's entertainment unit. He also formerly hosted and produced content for The National’s digital platforms. You can reach him at griffin.jaeger@cbc.ca

articles.title: 'I don't feel like a hero,' says Winnipeg woman who saved father, drowning toddler from Red River
articles.summary: A Winnipeg woman says she's still recovering, but glad everyone is safe, days after rescuing both a child who fell into the Red River and the girl's father, who attempted to save the child.

image.caption: Jayclyn Morrissette says she was on a walk with her neighbour at St. John's Park in Winnipeg last week when noticed a toddler 'flailing' in the Red River. (Submitted by Jayclyn Morrissette)

blocks.text: Manitoba·Updated
A Winnipeg woman says she's still recovering, but glad everyone is safe, days after rescuing both a child who fell into the Red River and the girl's father, who attempted to save the child.
'Selfless' woman jumped into action to save girl who fell into river near St. John's Park, police say
Jayclyn Morrissette, 32, was on a walk with her neighbour at St. John's Park, in Winnipeg's North End, on the evening of Aug. 24.
They stopped at a bench overlooking the Red River, where she "noticed a little girl flailing in the water," Morrissette told CBC on Wednesday.
She went down to the water as her neighbour went to the child's parents, who were frantically searching for the toddler, she said.
"I got down to the edge when the father had jumped in, and it took about 10 seconds before I realized he was not coming back up. So I … emptied my pockets and jumped in."
Trying to rescue the father was difficult, Morrissette said, so her neighbour grabbed her as she held onto him, and they were able to get the man out of the water.
Morrissette then swam back out to get the drowning toddler.
In a Wednesday morning news release detailing the incident, Winnipeg police said the rescuer swam backward toward the riverbank with the unconscious child on her chest.
"When I pulled her out, she was lifeless," Morrissette said. "As I was swimming back, I was also pumping her stomach."

items: Person in stable condition after being rescued from Red River in Winnipeg Thursday

blocks.text: Morrisette says she and her neighbour performed CPR — which she learned over a decade ago —on the child before first responders arrived.
The girl was taken to hospital in critical condition, where she was later stabilized, police said. She is now expected to make a full recovery.
But Morrissette said she suffered nightmares in the days following the incident.
"Her eyes were open and her tongue was purple, so that's all I could see every time I closed my eyes," Morrissette said. "I didn't sleep for a couple of days."

She also says once the adrenaline wore off, she realized she had suffered injuries to her neck and shoulder. She's been taking painkillers and is waiting to get testing, if her injuries do not get better.

Police did not release the child's age nor the names of the people involved, but said in their news release the woman who saved the girl and her father showed "remarkable courage and selflessness" in saving people who were strangers to her, with little regard for her own safety.
"I'm just a mom," Morrissette said. "I don't feel like a hero."
Someone else would have done the same thing in that situation, she said.
"I'm glad I was there. They're lucky I was there. I wish it just never happened," she said.
"Be safe. Watch your kids at all times. It only takes a second."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Ozten Shebahkeget is a member of Northwest Angle 33 First Nation who was born and raised in Winnipeg. She started writing for CBC Manitoba during the first Pathways program in 2022. She holds a master's degree in writing from the University of Saskatchewan.

articles.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
articles.summary: Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.

blocks.text: A woman, who was arrested for taking photos of jury members outside the courthouse in the Lindsay Clancy trial, has been charged with aggravated intimidation of a juror.

Dawn Light, 56, is accused of sitting in a restricted area outside the Plymouth courthouse and photographing jurors as they exited the building on Tuesday. Her lawyer called it a misunderstanding as she pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Lindsay Clancy, 36, is charged with the murders of her three children. The livestreamed trial has captured national and international media attention, and drawn strong, often deeply divided reactions from audiences.
The jury has been deliberating on the case since Thursday.
During Dawn Light's appearance in the court on Wednesday, Massachusetts lawyers said the sanctity of the judicial system was at risk because of her actions.

Light, a registered nurse with no prior criminal record, was ordered to stay away from the courthouse grounds and also from those associated with the Clancy trial. She was also ordered not to produce or disseminate photos that could have been preserved on iCloud.
Prosecutors requested a $50,000 (£37,000) cash bail, which was denied by the judge.
"This is a complete misunderstanding your honor. my client was trying to get a picture of Ms Clancy," Light's attorney Jennifer White said in court.
After the arraignment, a swarm of reporters gathered around Light. When one asked, "why did you want to see Lindsay [Clancy]", Light replied "why not?".
Authorities said they found Light in a restricted area in her parked car on Tuesday. When asked if she was taking videos, she said she was not and explained that she was waiting for Clancy.
Prosecutors alleged that when they went through Light's deleted folder on her phone they found photos of jurors exiting the courthouse, and Light was then taken into custody.
Prosecutors said the courthouse has taken extensive measures to protect the trial that has created a spectacle in the coastal Massachusetts town. They described Light's conduct as a serious matter.
Judge William Sullivan, who is overseeing the Clancy trial, has an order specifically prohibiting the photographing or filming of jurors.

The Plymouth, Massachusetts, jury has been deliberating since Thursday over whether Clancy is criminally responsible for killing her children. She is charged with three counts of first-degree murder and has pleaded not guilty.

articles.title: Germany: How to woo voters with an immigrant background
articles.summary: The number of voters in Germany with an immigrant background is rising. Yet the established parties barely manage to reach them. Why not?

image.caption: Do centrist parties in Germany not have the right messages for immigrant voters?Image: Emmanuele Contini/IMAGO

blocks.text: German voters of immigrant background are distancing themselves from the established parties even more than others, according to a study by the Berlin-based German Center for Integration and Migration Research (DeZIM).

In 2023, 12% of eligible voters in Germany were of immigration background — meaning they or at least one of their parents were born without German citizenship. That amounts to more than seven million people in a population of close to 84 million. But they are drifting away from the traditional centrist parties.

Nevertheless, according to the study, the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) continues to have the greatest voter potential among immigrants and their descendants: Two out of three voters with an immigrant background said they considered the SPD a viable option.
The center-right bloc of Christian Democratic Union and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) is close behind in second place. Only one in five respondents categorically rejected these parties.

"Older respondents with an immigrant background lean toward the SPD," said Friederike Römer, co-author of the study, at an online press conference this week. "This bond has been relatively strong in the past, but that seems to be breaking down now among younger generations."
Threat from the far right: Never quite German enough?
AfD targets migrants

Perhaps unsurprisingly, the anti-immigration Alternative for Germany (AfD) has the least potential voters of immigrant background. Nearly two-thirds of those surveyed said voting for the far-right was out of the question. People with roots in Turkey, the Middle East, and North Africa, in particular, reject the party, though the AfD does enjoy significant support among Germany's Russian community.

Nevertheless, the AfD is working to win over the immigrant voter base. "For a long time, it was the first party to communicate in immigrants' native languages using images that actually worked," said Martin Gerlach, federal executive director of the Turkish Community in Germany (TGD), recalling the AfD campaign in Berlin during the 2021 federal election. "It read: 'Atatürk would vote for the AfD.' Other parties simply don't bother to think about these target groups. That's crazy, because if you win over big segments of voters with a migration background, you win elections."
Safety a priority for immigrants

The TGD was active in 60 German cities ahead of the last federal election in February 2025, encouraging voters of Turkish background to cast their ballots. But Gerlach has noticed that immigrants are not inherently pro-immigration; on the contrary, there is widespread skepticism toward new immigrants or refugees, an issue that the AfD has seized on. This, he argues, is just one of many reasons why other parties are losing support among those voters.

"The political parties don't address safety at all, and that's a huge issue," he said. "Yet people in our community feel extremely threatened in many parts of Germany — they don't even dare go to the Baltic Sea coast," he added, referring to a series of xenophobic attacks in that region.

Gerlach believes that Islamophobia has a significant effect on voters from the Turkish community, but the centrist parties don't pay enough attention to it. "Anti-discrimination policy is seen in Germany as something progressive and left-wing, yet for the Turkish-origin community, it is about being protected by the constitution in the truest sense of the word," he said. "I believe this is a narrative that could win over a great many people."
Poorly treated? Racism in German medicine
Are the political parties missing a trick on social change?

Political scientist Özgür Özvatan pointed out that by 2030, more than half of Germany's population will have an immigrant background. He has also been critical of the established parties, most recently in his 2025 book "Every Vote Counts — Underestimated by Democrats, Courted by Populists: Migrant Germans as a Political Force."

"They are not reaching out to voters with an immigrant background the way they should — neither to recruit them for their own party, nor as volunteers, nor simply as voters," he said. "Sadly, we're missing the boat with this social change."

Özvatan argues that there is enormous potential to mobilize voters who have moved to Germany from authoritarian countries — people, for example, who have direct experience of trying to defend democracy. "We can tap into that if we enable them to obtain citizenship with voting rights as quickly as possible," he said.

The AfD, meanwhile, relies on a strategy of addressing the Turkish diaspora while establishing connections to the right-wing authoritarian President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan. Furthermore, he said, the AfD has become very skilled at pitting people with immigrant backgrounds against one another.

"A great deal of effort is being put into telling older immigrants: 'You are different from the newcomers, this whole debate about migration and deportation won't affect you.' And this tactic works well with those who do not reject the AfD," said Özvatan.
This article has been translated from German.

articles.title: Cops seize P7.51-M smuggled cigarettes in N. Mindanao
articles.summary: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Contraband couriers in Northern Mindanao watched millions go up in smoke without lighting a single match after back-to-back police intercepts yielded over P7.51 million worth of…

blocks.text: CAGAYAN DE ORO CITY — Contraband couriers in Northern Mindanao watched millions go up in smoke without lighting a single match after back-to-back police intercepts yielded over P7.51 million worth of smuggled cigarettes in less than 12 hours.

Authorities confiscated an exact total of P7,515,600 in illicit tobacco during separate law enforcement operations in Iligan City and Opol, Misamis Oriental, between the afternoon of Sept. 1 and the early hours of Sept. 2.

The first interdiction occurred around 4:50 p.m. on Sept. 1 along the National Highway at Purok 5, Sitio Mapalad, Barangay Dalipuga, Iligan City. Operatives from the City Intelligence Unit–City Special Operations Unit flagged down two Toyota Hi Ace vans — one white and one Silver Mica Metallic — at a checkpoint.

An inspection revealed 2,082 reams of “Modern” brand cigarettes valued at P1,665,600. The four vehicle occupants, all residents of Balo-i, Lanao del Norte, failed to produce importation clearances, Bureau of Customs (BOC) documents, tax stamps, or proof of tax duty payments.
The suspects claimed they were hired in Balo-i to haul the cargo from Marawi City to Cagayan de Oro City, claims police said remain subject to verification.
By 2 a.m. the following morning, a seaside tip-off triggered the second seizure along the coast of Barangay Barra in Opol, Misamis Oriental.

Alerted by an informant half an hour earlier, operatives from the Misamis Oriental Maritime Police Station, Opol Municipal Police, the BOC, and local barangay officials caught a 28-year-old suspect, alias “Ado,” unloading illicit cargo from an improvised floating device.
The beach intercept yielded 117 master cases holding 5,850 reams of Cannon Menthol 100s cigarettes, estimated at P5,850,000.
All seized items are slated for turnover to the Bureau of Customs for proper documentation and disposition.

Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay Jr., Police Regional Office-10 (PRO-10) director, credited the seizures to sustained, intelligence-led enforcement and inter-agency coordination, reiterating that regional units will maintain visible deterrence to halt the transit of untaxed goods across the region.

“We need strong intelligence, visible policing, and active community partnership to effectively prevent and suppress criminality. Our people can expect our units to remain vigilant and responsive against those who violate the law,” Babagay said. /das

articles.title: Marcos cites Presidential Airlift Wing
articles.summary: President Marcos has commended the men and women of the 250th Presidential Airlift Wing (PAW) for helping the government swiftly reach and deliver aid to the distressed during times of calamities.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 12:00am

President Marcos joins the Philippine Air Force in celebrating the 58th found- ing anniversary of the 250th Presidential Airlift Wing at Villamor Air Base in Pasay yesterday. The 250th PAW serves as the Air Force’s premier air mobility unit, providing transportation for the President and his family, visiting heads of state and other high-ranking dignitaries.
Ryan Baldemor

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has commended the men and women of the 250th Presidential Airlift Wing (PAW) for helping the government swiftly reach and deliver aid to the distressed during times of calamities.

Speaking at the 58th anniversary of the PAW yesterday, the President described the unit as the “multiplier” whose continuous training and modernization allowed it to respond safely and effectively to increasingly complex missions, including support for official engagements, emergency response or humanitarian operations.

“In these missions, you do more than just provide transportation. You help the government reach our people when they need us most,” Marcos said at the Philippine Air Force headquarters at the Villamor Air Base in Pasay City, citing his day-long inspection of flooded areas in Central Luzon yesterday.
From the 701st through 707th Special Mission Wing, the 250th PAW now “has been very much state-of-the-art,” the President said.
He presented awards and citations to officers and personnel for their exemplary service.

The 250th PAW is the Air Force’s premier air mobility unit, providing safe, secure, efficient and dignified air transportation for the President, First Family, visiting heads of state and other ranking dignitaries.

articles.title: DepEd to schools: Use AI tool for disaster preparedness
articles.summary: Education Secretary Sonny Angara has ordered public school administrators, teachers and disaster response coordinators nationwide to integrate LIGTAS+ into their disaster preparedness routines as…

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 12:00am
Lahar inundates Sta. Fe National High School in San Marcelino, Zambales yesterday.
Noel Pabalete

MANILA, Philippines — Education Secretary Sonny Angara has ordered public school administrators, teachers and disaster response coordinators nationwide to integrate LIGTAS+ into their disaster preparedness routines as hundreds of schools remain affected by flooding and other disasters.

According to Angara, LIGTAS+ or the Learning Institution Geohazard Tracking and Assessment for Safety would allow school leaders to identify risks earlier and make timely decisions before hazards disrupt classes and other school operations.

“We can’t just wait for a storm or earthquake to strike before we act. With LIGTAS+, we can anticipate risks early so our school leaders can make timely, informed decisions before hazards turn into emergencies. What we need is clear and reliable information for earlier preparation,” he said.

Developed by DepEd’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Service and the Education Center for AI Research, LIGTAS+ combines artificial intelligence, weather forecasts, satellite radar imagery and data from government and international scientific agencies to provide school-level hazard alerts.

In a separate event, Angara accompanied President Marcos in inspecting flood-affected schools in Tarlac, Zambales and Pampanga, where the combined impact of the southwest monsoon and recent tropical cyclones damaged at least 622 schools and 4,025 classrooms.
Of the damaged classrooms, 946 were destroyed, 806 sustained major damage and 2,274 suffered minor damage.
The DepEd estimated that P2.9 billion would be needed for response and recovery efforts in Central Luzon.

articles.title: Pilandok exits today
articles.summary: Tropical Storm Pilandok is set to exit the Philippine area of responsibility today, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration said.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 12:00am

As of 4 p.m. yesterday, Pilandok was located 1,080 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, packing winds of 65 kilometers per hour and gusts of up to 80 kph while moving west-northwestward at 10 kph.
PAGASA

MANILA, Philippines — Tropical Storm Pilandok is set to exit the Philippine area of responsibility today, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said.
PAGASA said Pilandok will maintain its strength as a tropical storm and move northwestward until it exits PAR early today.
Despite the exit, occasional rains will still be felt in Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Zambales and Bataan due to the southwest monsoon.
Death toll at 39
The death toll from weather-related incidents since Aug. 1 climbed to 39 after the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC) reported five more fatalities yesterday.

Three of the latest fatalities were from Zambales, including two people who died in a landslide on the Morong, Bataan side of the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority and another in a separate landslide in Olongapo.
Two other deaths were reported in Pampanga, involving a landslide and a nipa hut that was swept away by strong currents, both in Porac.
The NDRRMC said the latest casualties were attributed to the combined effects of typhoons Luis, Maymay and Neneng and the southwest monsoon since Aug. 1.
Benguet recorded the highest number of deaths with 15, followed by Rizal and Batangas with four each.
Caloocan City had three fatalities, while Quezon and Occidental Mindoro had two each.
La Union, Pangasinan, Oriental Mindoro and Negros Occidental each recorded one death.
Also included in the death toll were passengers of a Toyota Avanza that plunged into the Tarlac River after a portion of the Agana Bridge in Tarlac City collapsed on Aug. 29.
The body of passenger Shanen Tuhao, a resident of Cavite, was found floating in the river in Barangay San Vicente, Bayambang, Pangasinan at around 4 p.m. on Sept. 1.
Before Shanen, the remains of another passenger, James Patrick Taborlupa, was recovered on Aug. 31 in Barangay Carael, Lingayen, Pangasinan.
Two other passengers, Sheila Mae Taborlupa and Paul Harvey Collado, remain missing.

Following the incident in Tarlac, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon has ordered a nationwide structural audit of all national bridges following continuous downpours that led to the collapse of two bridges in Tarlac province last week. – Michael Punongbayan, Adrian Kenneth Halili, Ramon Efren Lazaro, Ric Sapnu, Rainier Allan Ronda, Emmanuel Tupas

articles.title: Coded emojis facilitate dark web drug trade – lawmaker
articles.summary: The lucrative illegal drug industry has leveled up operations with innovations using digital technology, as social media entices more followers to the illegal trade.

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 12:00am

“Social media has made it possible for drug dealers to operate in plain sight. They can use coded words, images, emojis and seemingly harmless posts to advertise illegal drugs while trying to evade the platforms’ detection systems,” he observed.
MANILA, Philippines — The lucrative illegal drug industry has leveled up operations with innovations using digital technology, as social media entices more followers to the illegal trade.

Las Piñas Rep. Mark Anthony Santos, chairman of the dangerous drugs committee of the House of Representatives, cited studies showing how social media platforms have been used to facilitate illegal drug transactions.

He said Instagram has “emerged as a significant platform for online drug trafficking,” with experienced users reportedly able to locate dealers through seemingly ordinary posts, accounts and interactions.

According to Santos, drug dealers have also used emojis as coded advertisements for illegal drugs – for example, using symbols or images associated with particular drugs to avoid automated content filters.
Santos said such tactics demonstrate the difficulty of relying solely on automated moderation to prevent online drug trafficking.

articles.title: Impeachment court eyes whole-day trial
articles.summary: The Senate impeachment court may hold whole-day trials in October as senators juggle their duties as judges trying Vice President Sara Duterte and as senators scrutinizing next year’s proposed…

blocks.text: September 3, 2026 | 12:00am

Office of the Vice President Assistant Secretary and Assistant Chief of Staff Lemuel Ortonio, the second hostile witness, responds to questions from counsel to prosecution Mae Divinagracia during direct examination on the 18th day of the impeachment trial at the Senate in Pasay on Aug. 25, 2026.
The Philippine STAR / Ryan Baldemor /

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court may hold whole-day trials in October as senators juggle their duties as judges trying Vice President Sara Duterte and as senators scrutinizing next year’s proposed P7.2-trillion budget.

Before adjourning Day 21 of the trial yesterday, presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero informed parties of the possible grueling schedule on Oct. 1, 2, 5 to 9 and 12 to 15, from 10 a.m. to “early evening” and “on some occasion, exceed dinner time.”
There will be no trial during the interim between Oct. 16 and Nov. 6 to give way to budget committee hearings, as well as the Undas break.

Trial will resume on Nov. 9 and 16, but only from 10 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., then “proceed to normal programming” starting Nov. 23 “until we finish the case” by December, the court’s target verdict date, according to Escudero.
“This is a heads-up that time may come that we will have a whole-day trial, so we can dispense one to three witnesses per trial date,” Escudero said.
Defense lawyers said they are ready for the new schedule.
Sen. JV Ejercito said the new setup may be “the best solution” for senators to don their hats as jurors and as lawmakers to have committee and plenary debates on the outlay.
“The problem is it’s either we finish impeachment or else we have a reenacted budget,” Ejercito said.
Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri said he is feeling the toll of working for 12 hours a day.
Impeachment court spokesman Reginald Tongol said another setup being looked into would allow senators to attend budget hearings while trial is ongoing as part of the “continuing quorum” rule.

During yesterday’s plenary session, senators approved Zubiri’s motion for the suspension of Senate rules to allow senators to still be declared present for the plenary session while attending budget committee hearings.
– Bella Cariaso

articles.title: Senate OKs bill barring public execs’ kin from government contracts
articles.summary: The Senate unanimously approved on third and final reading a bill barring relatives of public officials up to the fourth civil degree of consanguinity and affinity from securing government contracts,…

Senate of the Philippines.
Graphics by Philstar.com / Enrico Alonzo

MANILA, Philippines — The Senate unanimously approved on third and final reading a bill barring relatives of public officials up to the fourth civil degree of consanguinity and affinity from securing government contracts, a measure prompted by recent anomalies in public infrastructure projects.
Voting 15-0 with no abstentions on yesterday, lawmakers passed Senate Bill No. 1962, authored by Sen. Francis Escudero.

The measure, which he filed while he was still Senate president in July last year, explicitly disqualifies officials’ relatives from state procurements and provides corresponding penalties for violations.
During the session yesterday, Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said the bill was drafted in direct response to recent controversies.

“And the intention of the bill is to prevent circumvention of some families to corner construction contracts in DPWH and other infrastructure agencies,” he said, referring to the Department of Public Works and Highways.

Sen. Juan Miguel Zubiri said the ban should firmly apply to “Pharmally-type deals,” stressing that the law should prevent politicians and public servants from “supplying medicines and all sorts of materials to government.”

articles.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with King Charles and relatively new Prime…

image.caption: The King was due to give a speech before the group went to the unveiling of the exhibit alongside other dignitaries and some schoolchildrenImage: Adrian Dennis/REUTERS

blocks.text: French President Emmanuel Macron began a two-day trip to the UK by visiting another famous new arrival from France, the Bayeux Tapestry, with King Charles III and Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
Macron and his wife Brigitte, and Burnham and his wife Marie-France van Heel joined King Charles and Queen Camilla to walk the length of the 70-meter tapestry in the British Museum.

blocks.caption: The Bayeux Tapestry depicts the events of 1066, a defining date in the passage of British history and in the creation of the modern French-infused English languageImage: Pascal Deloche/Godong/picture alliance

blocks.text: Why is the Bayeux Tapestry in London?

The tapestry, which depicts the momentous events of 1066 culminating in William the Conqueror of Normandy claiming the English throne, is on temporary loan from its usual home in France. It's the first time it's touched British soil since its creation in the 11th century.
The embroidery is on loan for a 10-month exhibiton opening to the public next week, on September 10. The exchange was first announced during Macron's state visit last year.

Though it's thought to have been made in the British Isles, it had been on French soil ever since the 11th century. It's usually on show in Bayeux in Normandy in northern France, hence the name. The effectively priceless artefact was transited across the Channel in secret in July.
Prime Minister Burnham, who took office six weeks ago, called the tapestry's return "a landmark moment" in the history of the two countries.

He also hailed ties with Macron's French government more generally in the House of Commons on Wednesday, alluding to reduced illegal migration crossings of the English Channel — a bid to counter one of Reform UK's favorite summer talking points.
"The loaning of the tapestry is a great example of French-British cooperation — the same cooperation that has helped us reduce summer small boat crossings to a seven-year low," Burnham said.
It's Macron's first UK visit since Burnham took office and their first in-person meeting as leaders.

blocks.caption: Moving the artefact from its usual home in Bayeux to Britain was a painstaking process months in the makingImage: Lou Benoist/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: What is the Bayeux Tapestry?
The Bayeux Tapestry is a 70-meter long artwork, which is thought to be incomplete, depicting the Norman conquest of England in 1066.

Norman forces led by William the Conqueror were able to defeat and dethrone King Harold Godwinson in a campaign culminating in victory at the Battle of Hastings. The tapestry famously depicts Harold being shot in the eye with an arrow, as he is said to have died — admittedly in what modern historians believe is likely a myth or artistic exaggeration.

This conquest was a crucial contributing moment in the establishment of what would become England and later the British Empire and the UK. It was the last of several successful foreign invasions of England in a millenium, and turned out to be the last one for a millenium.
The conquest also added the final core ingredient, French, to the linguistic melting pot that produced the modern English language.

The embroidered cloth, which has brief Latin titles captioning its 58 scenes, is widely accepted to have been made in England as a tribute to William after his victory. It was then transported to his family home in Normandy.

blocks.caption: England's last Anglo-Saxon King Harold Godwinson saw off the Norse viking King Harald Hardrada at the Battle of Stamford Bridge in 1066, but riding south to deal with William the Conqueror soon after proved a battle too farImage: Pascal Deloche/Godong/picture alliance

articles.title: Climate change will pass key 1.5 C limit, UN report says while charting path to bringing levels back down
articles.summary: In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of the worst of global warming's harms. Officials say…

image.caption: People look on from the observation deck of the CN Tower as smoke from forest fires in Northwestern Ontario blankets Toronto in July. (Cole Burston/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Science

In a strategic retreat in the fight against climate change, the United Nations has acknowledged that Earth has lost its chance to prevent some of the worst of global warming's harms. Officials say the world must now figure out how to get temperatures below the danger zone and back to safety.
The worst climate impacts are now unavoidable, as warming will at least reach 1.8 C: UN

The planet will soon exceed the safe temperature threshold agreed upon in the 2015 Paris climate accord because of warming from the burning of coal, oil and gas, according to a bleak first-of-its-kind report issued by the United Nations Environment Programme Wednesday.

Instead of giving up, scientists and UN officials recommend trying to limit excessive warming and then bring the temperature back down to the agreed-upon threshold. But it still will mean decades of increased weather-related disasters, rising seas, extinctions and melting ice and glaciers.
"Humanity is speeding past the limit to avoid climate catastrophe," United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said.
If we've missed the 1.5-degree climate target, what’s next?
After a period of over-the-limit warming, the new strategy envisions getting back below the limit by ending fossil fuel use and developing some way to suck industries' carbon dioxide out of the air.

"It's a reality check. We have to live with this warmer world," said report co-author Richard Betts, a climate scientist at the University of Exeter. "But there's still a lot we can do to limit warming."

items: 'Super' El Niño didn't cause this year's fires and heat waves, but it's about to take us on a 'wild ride'
'Just stop burning fossil fuels.' Scientists stress that our smoky skies have only one true fix

blocks.text: Passing the warming threshold

After the Paris climate accord, the United Nations ordered its climate science arm to study different warming limits. Scientists generally accepted a limit of 1.5 C above mid-19th century temperatures, after finding dramatic impacts that affect people and the planet at 2 C but not at 1.5 C.
The world is now at 1.4 C above pre-industrial levels, some scientists have calculated. The measure is based on a 20-year average, rather than a single year's temperatures.

Despite experts saying there's no way to limit warming to 1.5 C, UN officials long maintained the 1.5 C window was still open. Wednesday's report finally admitted that the world will cross the 1.5 threshold "in the next few years."

The report said the most optimistic scenario has warming peaking at 1.8 C around mid-century if countries pursue ambitious climate goals, but that governments' current policies should push temperatures to 2.6 C above pre-industrial levels by 2100.
The UN said it wants policymakers to "prepare for and navigate a future'' in which the globe crosses that limit and then corrects course and cools temperatures.

The report envisions that after exceeding 1.5 C, global temperatures will follow a hump-shaped path of more warming, peak, then gradually cool to below the 1.5 C mark, ideally by the end of the century. The report and experts call it "overshoot."
"Let's be very clear, 1.5 target is still the goal. But now we need to approach it differently from above," said UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen.

The 1.5 C limit is not "some magical climate cliff" where it's just game over, said University of Victoria climate scientist Andrew Weaver, who wasn't part of the study. "Every tenth of a degree we avoid still means less damage."
Limiting how high temps go past threshold is key
It's most important to first limit the new peak temperature and then reduce the amount of time above 1.5 C, Andersen said.
But the world likely will be in that overshoot period for "many, many decades," Betts said.
Every five years' delay in reducing emissions adds at least a tenth of a degree to peak warming, said report co-author Joeri Rogelj, a climate scientist at Imperial College London.
"If we act now we can limit overshoot," the report said. "Not a safe world, but safer than remaining above" 1.5 C for the long term.
"This is among the bleakest UN climate reports I have read. It carries the unmistakable tone of desperation, frustration and urgency — but not resignation," Weaver said.

items: Canada joins first summit focused on moving away from fossil fuels
Public funding for fossil fuel industry breaks another Liberal climate promise, advocates say

blocks.text: Adapting to a deadlier, hungrier, thirstier world
Governments need to increase efforts to adapt to worsening warming, which hits the poor hardest, "because some impacts simply cannot be avoided," Andersen said.
The report calls this phase "coping and containment."

During this overshoot period, more people will die or get sick because of the worsening climate change and its extreme weather, the report said. Food production will drop, people will go hungry, water shortages will worsen, economies will be hurt and species like coral will go extinct.

Although the triggers behind the recent deadly Nepal flooding that came as part of a Himalayan glacier dislodging are complex, Betts said "unfortunately we do expect to see more of such things and this is exactly why we need to limit peak warming."

The report warns of "tipping points" with irreversible and cascading effects, including the loss of the West Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets, the loss of the Amazon rainforest and the shutdown of the Atlantic Ocean circulation system that keeps much of Europe warm.
"Some locations might become more or less uninsurable or even uninhabitable," the report said.

The last phase in overshoot is cooling the planet by removing carbon dioxide from the air and storing it somewhere. The report said the traditional approach of this is planting more trees, but it says planting trees could, at most, shave a tenth of a degree off global temperatures. So the authors said more novel carbon removal approaches will be needed.
Other scientists called that unreliable and expensive.
"We were unable to stop the runaway train of global emissions to avoid 1.5 C of warming," said Stanford University climate scientist Rob Jackson, who wasn't part of the report.
"Now overshoot scenarios require us to stop the train quickly and to back it up. Is it our best hope? Absolutely. Is it likely? Absolutely not."

articles.title: Sara Duterte impeachment trial Day 21: Poa faces hostile witness grilling as trial lawyers clash
articles.summary: The 21st day of Vice President Sara Duterte"s impeachment trial opened with private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. describing former Department of Education (DepEd) Undersecretary and witness Michael…

blocks.text: Published September 2, 2026 11:55pm

The 21st day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial opened with private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa Jr. describing former Department of Education (DepEd) Undersecretary and witness Michael Poa as an “abogadong walang alam,” a remark that was later stricken from the record.

Tolosa said the prosecution was presenting Poa’s testimony that he was made to respond to state auditors’ queries about DepEd’s use of confidential funds, despite Poa’s repeated statements in previous hearings that he had no personal knowledge of how the funds were disbursed.
Defense team lead counsel Sheila Sison objected to such characterization of Poa, who is her co-counsel in the defense team.
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero ruled in favor of Sison and ordered the phrase stricken from the record, saying it was “discourteous, to say the least.”
After this exchange, Escudero declared Poa as a hostile witness, allowing Tolosa to ask leading questions.

During Tolosa’s direct examination of Poa about the P15 million confidential fund that DepEd spent for paying informants, Poa testified that purchasing information from informants using confidential funds does not guarantee success in information gathering.

"Unang-una, hindi kailangan na kapag bumili ka ng information, necessarily, 'pag nakuha mo 'yung information, it will result in success," Poa said when private prosecutor Benjamin Tolosa, Jr. asked if evidence of success is required in the purchase of information as provided under Joint Circular 2015-01, which governs the use of confidential and intelligence funds.
This answer by Poa, however, only came after lengthy arguments between Tolosa and Sison, who registered multiple objections to the supposedly misleading questions.
This prompted Escudero to appeal to the public and the senator-judges to be more patient.

“Para sa kaalaman din po ng kapwa ko senator-judges at mga sumusubaybay, mahirap na nga po na may dalawang abogadong nagkakaroon ng tagisan ng talino, gawin pa nating tatlo. Kaya pag-unawa lang po at pasensya ang hinihiling namin,” the presiding officer said.

(For the information of my fellow senator-judges and those watching the proceedings, it is difficult enough for two lawyers to have a battle of wits, let alone three. So we just ask for understanding and patience.)

Later, Poa testified that he did not ask DepEd special disbursing officer Eduard Fajarda whether he himself was disbursing the confidential funds. Poa also said he did not ask whether the rewards paid to informants had resulted in successful information gathering.
Poa also reiterated that he has no personal knowledge of how the confidential fund was used.

After Poa was discharged from the witness stand, Escudero granted the prosecution’s request for the court to issue a subpoena or order to three individuals to testify before the Senate impeachment court.
The subpoenas were for Commission on Audit’s (COA) Bresilio Sabaldan, former Assistant Secretary Sunshine Cherry Fajarda of the Department of Education, and Police Major Jovelyn Magay.
In addition, Escudero also discussed the possible adjusted schedule of the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Under the proposed schedule, on October 1 and 2; October 5 to 9; and October 12 to 15, the trial will be for the entire day, from 10 a.m. up until early evening.

Before the trial started, House prosecutor Joel Chua of Manila said that the prosecution is considering dropping the bribery charge under Article 3 of the impeachment case against Vice President Duterte.

He was referring to the impeachment Article which alleges that the Vice President must be impeached for committing bribery by giving monetary gifts or payments to Department of Education (DepEd) officials to induce the violation and circumvention of procurement and other related laws.
Chua said such a move is being considered because the prosecution does not want a protracted hearing. He stressed that there is no final decision yet on the matter. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians
articles.summary: Iranian media reports two children were among those killed when shrapnel hit a home. Iran then launched missiles and drones at US targets in the Middle East.
articles.byline: Joe Coughlan, Claire Keenan, David Gritten

blocks.text: Watch: Iran and US exchange air strikes
ByJoe CoughlanClaire Keenan and David Gritten
Iran has accused the US of a war crime after officials said a missile strike killed four people including two children at a wedding celebration.

The Iranian Red Crescent Society (IRCS) said shrapnel from a missile hit a family wedding ceremony at a home in southern Iran, causing the deaths. Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei called the incident a "war crime".
A US Central Command (Centcom) spokesperson said it "never targets civilians", adding that it was aware of the reports.
Iranian authorities said another 14 people were killed elsewhere. In response, Iran launched missiles and drones at US targets in Jordan, Kuwait, Iraq and Bahrain.
Most of the drones and missiles Iran launched at neighbouring countries were reportedly intercepted. Kuwait said a drone started a fire in a residential complex but caused no casualties.

Centcom said strikes on Iran followed "recent attempted attacks" by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against American forces and commercial shipping in the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway, through which around 20% of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.
The Iranian military's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that operations against American forces in the region would continue until the US "regrets" its crimes.
Image source, Iranian Red Crescent Society
A picture distributed by the Iranian Red Crescent Society reportedly showing the remains of a building which was hosting the wedding ceremony
US President Donald Trump described Tuesday's strikes on Iran as "large and powerful".
Centcom said the targets included air defence sites, radar systems and maritime assets.
Iranian media reported explosions across the southern provinces of Hormozgan, Sistan-Baluchestan, Kerman and Khuzestan.
The IRCS said at least four people were killed and 67 others were injured when shrapnel from a missile hit a family wedding ceremony at a home in the coastal town of Kuhestak, in Sirik.
Citing the Hormozgan Governorate, Iranian media named the dead as Zarkhatoon Taheri, 50; Kolsum Mallahi Nazhdnia, 43; Mohammad Mallahi, 16; and Amirali Karimi, four.
Media outlets initially quoted the IRCS as saying that five people were killed.

"Unfortunately, this is a residential building. And unfortunately, this happened during my daughter's wedding ceremony," Ali Mallahi, father of the bride and owner of the building, said in a video broadcast by state TV.
"It is a very saddening incident... Thank God the casualties were not higher."
Iran's parliamentary speaker and top negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, said it was another attack showing the US was "Satan".
Watch: What we know about reported strike on Iran wedding celebrations

BBC Verify confirmed that a video and two images taken on Tuesday near Kuhestak's coast showed the destruction of a telecommunications tower, and that other videos from Tuesday and Wednesday showed severely damaged houses about 130m (427ft) north of the tower.
BBC Persian Forensics, by examining published videos and CCTV footage, found the telecommunications tower was about 112m (367 ft) from the house where the wedding was being held.

A weapons expert also told BBC Verify that footage purportedly from the scene appeared to show remnants of an AGM-84 Standoff Land Attack Missile (SLAM_ER) - a type of cruise missile known to be used by the US.
Centcom spokesman Captain Tim Hawkins told the BBC it was aware of reports from Iranian state media of the attack in Sirik.
He added: "The US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC."
Iranian state media reported that another seven people were killed in three separate US strikes around Ahvaz and Aqajari, in Khuzestan.

The IRGC meanwhile said that four members of its aerospace force, which oversees Iran's ballistic missiles, were killed by US attacks in Kermanshah, and that three members of the paramilitary Basij Resistance Force were killed on Lavan island, in the Gulf.

blocks.caption: Map of Strait of Hormuz

blocks.text: Early on Wednesday, the IRGC and the regular Iranian military announced that they had launched ballistic missiles and drones towards US bases in Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates in retaliation for the US strikes.
They said the attacks caused casualties and damage at the US Marine barracks at Camp Titin on Jordan's Gulf of Aqaba coast.
Reuters news agency cited US officials as saying there were no casualties.
The Jordanian Armed Forces said they engaged 13 ballistic missiles, 10 of which were destroyed and three of which fell in remote, uninhabited areas.

The IRGC and the Iranian military also said that a maintenance centre, warehouses and equipment belonging to the US military were destroyed in Irbil, in Iraq's northern Kurdistan region, according to state media. Iraqi authorities did not comment on the attack, but local media reported that a US surveillance balloon was hit by drones.
In Kuwait, the fire service said its crews put out a fire at a residential complex that was struck by a drone and that no casualties were reported.
In a separate incident, the IRGC said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines while being guided through an "illegal route" in the Strait of Hormuz by the US military.
Saudi Arabia's national shipping company said two Filipino sailors were killed "in a security incident" involving its crude oil tanker SIDR as the vessel transited the waterway on Monday.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Vessels were visible across the Strait of Hormuz from Oman this week

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Vessels were visible across the Strait of Hormuz from Oman this week

After about a month-long pause, the US resumed attacks on Iran on Sunday, when it announced it had struck two rocket launchers to prevent them being used to lay naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran retaliated by firing missiles at air bases in Jordan and a drone at the UAE.

The US and Israel launched a joint attack on Iran on 28 February, killing the country's supreme leader and other top officials at the start of a massive air campaign. Iran responded by attacking Israel, US bases and allied states in the Gulf with missiles and drones, and effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.

In June, the US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) that called for an end to hostilities on all fronts and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. It also gave them two months to reach a final deal that covers Iran's nuclear programme, US sanctions and a permanent truce.
However, the MoU collapsed within weeks, leading to a resumption of hostilities.

Since then, both US and Iranian forces have fired on commercial shipping in the region, with Iran targeting vessels it says have sought to transit the Strait of Hormuz without its permission and the US enforcing a naval blockade of Iranian ports.
Last week, the US had indicated that it was switching to economic sanctions on Iran, rather than military options, to try to win concessions and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian officials and state media have largely dismissed the campaign as a continuation of previous US economic measures.
Additional reporting by BBC Persian
Six months into the Iran war: What has Trump accomplished?
